- [Cold Email Infrastructure Setup](https://imisofts.com/email-infrastructure): Domains, inboxes, SPF, DKIM, DMARC and warm-up built so your cold email reaches the inbox. Sending in about 14 days.

  Your Copy Is Not the Problem. Your Infrastructure Is. We build the sending layer underneath your outbound: domains, mailboxes, authentication, warm-up and monitoring, set up to satisfy what Google, Yahoo and Microsoft now enforce. Illustrative domain health view. Yours is monitored continuously.
  What is cold email infrastructure, and why do campaigns fail without it?
  Cold email infrastructure is everything underneath the message: the domains you send from, the mailboxes on them, the DNS records that prove you are who you say you are, the warm-up that builds sending reputation, and the monitoring that catches a problem before it burns a domain. It stopped being optional. Google, Yahoo and Microsoft all now require bulk senders to authenticate with SPF, DKIM and DMARC, keep spam complaints under 0.3 percent, and offer one-click unsubscribe. Microsoft joined enforcement in April 2025 and by May 2026 all three are enforcing in production. The part that catches teams out: failures are rejections, not spam folders. Google and Microsoft now issue permanent 550 rejections for non-compliant bulk mail. Your email is not quietly filtered where you might notice a low reply rate. It is bounced at the SMTP level and never delivered at all. Meanwhile Google's own guidance is to stay under 0.1 percent complaints and never touch 0.3, because once you spike past it, deliverability degrades and recovers slowly. So the sequence matters: buy and configure domains properly, authenticate all three records, warm mailboxes gradually, keep lists clean, and monitor placement continuously. We build that layer and then keep watching it. It pairs with cold email campaigns and B2B lead generation when you want the campaigns run too. Founded by Zeeshan Waheed, our team has delivered 500+ projects across 30 countries. Provider requirements were verified in July 2026 and do change. We track them as part of the managed plan.
  Why sending on day one is how domains get burned
  Reputation is earned gradually and lost instantly. This is the sequence we run, and skipping any step is the most common reason a perfectly good offer gets no replies. Illustrative sequence. Timelines vary with volume.

- [Cold Email for SaaS](https://imisofts.com/cold-email-saas): Dedicated sending infrastructure and SaaS-specific sequences that reach technical buyers and book demos. Sending in about 14 days.

  Fill the Demo Calendar With Buyers Who Ignore Vendor Email. We build the sending infrastructure, write sequences that speak to CTOs and heads of product rather than to everyone, and run the campaigns through to a booked demo. Illustrative dashboard. Yours reports on your own sends.
  Why does SaaS cold email fail, and what actually fixes it?
  Two things kill it, and only one of them is the copy. The first is that the mail never arrives. The second is that when it does arrive, it reads like it could have been sent to anyone. Deliverability stopped being a dark art in February 2024, when Google and Yahoo published enforceable requirements for bulk senders, followed by Microsoft in 2025. If you send at volume you now need SPF, DKIM and DMARC aligned on the sending domain, one-click unsubscribe under RFC 8058 honoured within two days, and a spam complaint rate held below 0.30%, with 0.10% the level worth actually targeting. Miss those and mail is rejected outright with a 550 error. It does not quietly land in a spam folder where you might eventually notice it. Speed of reply matters as much as the reply itself. Harvard Business Review research by Oldroyd, McElheran and Elkington found companies that contacted a web lead within an hour were about seven times more likely to have a meaningful conversation with a decision maker than those that waited just one hour longer, and more than sixty times more likely than those that waited a day. In the same study only 37% of firms managed to respond within an hour. Outbound has the same physics: a warm reply that sits for two days is a cold lead again. So we build both halves. Dedicated email infrastructure separate from your product and billing mail, then sequences written around the specific problem your software removes. It sits alongside our wider cold email campaigns and B2B lead generation work. Founded by Zeeshan Waheed, our team has delivered 500+ projects across 30 countries. Sender requirements are from Google, Yahoo and Microsoft published guidance. The response-time research is Harvard Business Review, March 2011. Neither figure is a claim about our results.

- [Cold Email for Recruiters](https://imisofts.com/cold-email-recruiters): Separate outbound systems for business development and candidate sourcing, so recruiters can win clients and fill roles at the same time.

  Why does recruiter outreach underperform, and what changes it?
  Recruitment is the most saturated outbound market there is, and most firms make it harder by running both of their audiences through one channel and one sender reputation. You are selling to two completely different people. A hiring manager needs to hear about time to fill, quality of shortlist and the cost of the role sitting open. A passive candidate needs to hear about the role, the team and the money, and does not care about your placement statistics at all. Industry benchmarks put average time to fill at roughly 42 days, with technical roles running considerably longer, so the vacancy you are pitching against has usually been open a while and the hiring manager is already irritated by it. Sending both from one setup is the mistake that costs most. Candidate sourcing generates more complaints than any other kind of outbound, because people who are not job hunting mark it as spam. If that traffic shares a domain with your business development mail, one bad sourcing week takes your client outreach down with it. Since February 2024 Google and Yahoo have enforced a hard complaint ceiling of 0.30% for bulk senders, with Microsoft following for high-volume senders in 2025, and mail that breaches it is rejected with a permanent 550 error rather than filed to spam. So we build two. Separate authenticated domains, separate warm-up, one shared suppression list so an opt-out on either side is honoured on both. Same email infrastructure foundation as our wider cold email campaigns and B2B lead generation work. Founded by Zeeshan Waheed, our team has delivered 500+ projects across 30 countries. Time to fill is an industry benchmark and varies widely by role and sector. Sender requirements are from Google, Yahoo and Microsoft published guidance. Neither is a claim about our results.

### AI voice agents, AI calling and AI receptionists

- [AI Voice Agents](https://imisofts.com/ai-voice-agents): AI voice agents that call and follow up with your leads in under a minute. Consent capture, DNC scrubbing and opt-out handling built in. Live in 2 to 4 weeks.

  Your Leads Get Called in 60 Seconds. Legally. We build AI voice agents that call, qualify and follow up with your leads around the clock, with consent capture, DNC scrubbing and opt-out handling wired in before the first call is ever placed. Illustrative interface. Your build runs in your own CRM.
  What is an AI voice agent, and who should build yours?
  An AI voice agent places and answers real phone calls in a natural voice. It reaches a new lead within about a minute, asks your qualifying questions, books the appointment on your calendar, and follows up as many times as you tell it to, at any hour. Most teams get one thing wrong: the agent is the easy half. In the US, outbound calling is governed by the TCPA and the exposure is counted per call. An AI that dials thousands of numbers a day scales a compliance mistake exactly as fast as it scales your pipeline. So who should build yours? Someone who ships the compliance layer and the agent as one system. Consent captured and logged at the source. National DNC and your internal opt-out list scrubbed upstream, so a suppressed number physically cannot reach the dialer. Opt-outs honored instantly across calls and texts. A2P 10DLC on the messaging leg. A live person taking over the moment real buying intent appears. That is what we build at imisofts. Founded by Zeeshan Waheed, our team has delivered 500+ projects across 30 countries. This page is not legal advice. Confirm your specific setup with a telecom attorney.
  A suppressed number physically cannot reach the dialer
  Most teams bolt an AI onto their CRM and hope. We put the gate upstream, so the agent only ever sees numbers it is allowed to call. That is the difference between a growth engine and a liability machine. Illustrative flow. Wired into your CRM workflow.

- [TCPA-Compliant AI Calling Setup](https://imisofts.com/tcpa-compliant-ai-calling): We build the consent, DNC and opt-out layer under your AI dialer, plus A2P 10DLC registration and an audit-ready record. Live in 2 to 4 weeks.

  Dial at Volume Without Betting the Company. We build the consent, suppression and opt-out layer underneath your AI dialer, so a number you are not allowed to call physically cannot be called. Illustrative compliance record. Yours lives in your own CRM.
  What does TCPA-compliant AI calling actually require?
  TCPA-compliant AI calling means the consent, suppression and opt-out layer is built into your dialing system, not bolted on afterwards. The AI itself is never the legal problem. Calling someone without consent, or failing to honor a stop request, is. The exposure is counted per call, which is why volume makes it dangerous: $500 per violation and up to $1,500 per willful call or text under 47 U.S.C. section 227. A system placing thousands of calls a day multiplies a setup mistake at exactly that rate. What actually changed recently, because most pages still get this wrong. The FCC's one-to-one consent rule was vacated by the Eleventh Circuit in January 2025, so shared-form lead consent was not outlawed the way many vendors claimed. Separately, the FCC's broad revocation rule, the one requiring an opt-out to apply across all of a sender's messages, was delayed again in January 2026 and now takes effect on 31 January 2027. What is already in force is simpler and stricter than people assume: a consumer can revoke consent by any reasonable means, including just telling your agent to stop. So the build that keeps you safe is unglamorous: capture consent provably, scrub every list upstream, honor revocation instantly in any form it arrives, register your messaging, and keep a record you could hand to a regulator. That is what we set up. Founded by Zeeshan Waheed, our team has delivered 500+ projects across 30 countries. This page is information, not legal advice, and rules change. Confirm your specific setup with a telecom attorney before you dial.
  The check happens before the dialer, not after
  Most teams scrub lists on a schedule and hope nothing slips through between runs. We put the gate in the path of the call itself, so a suppressed number is blocked at the moment of dialing and the block is logged. Illustrative flow. Wired into your calling workflow.

  What does an AI receptionist do for a dental or medical practice?
  Three things that decide practice revenue: it answers the calls your front desk cannot get to, it reduces the appointments that quietly evaporate, and it fills the gaps when someone cancels. No-shows are the expensive one. US dental practices average roughly 15 to 20 percent no-show rates, which works out to something like $120,000 to $240,000 in lost production a year for a typical practice. Medical practices average around 20 percent, and missed appointments cost the wider US healthcare system an estimated $150 billion annually. The fix is unglamorous and well evidenced. Text reminders alone reduce no-shows by roughly 20 to 30 percent, and multi-channel sequences combining phone, text and email reach 30 to 45 percent. The reason most practices do not get that result is not that they disagree, it is that nobody at the desk has time to run a disciplined sequence on every patient, every week, forever. That is exactly the kind of work that should not depend on a human remembering. - [AI Speed-to-Lead for Mortgage Lenders](https://imisofts.com/ai-calling-mortgage-lending): Call every mortgage lead in under 60 seconds, compliantly. Consent capture, DNC scrubbing and litigator screening built in.

  First Lender to Call Usually Wins the Loan. We build an AI agent that contacts every new mortgage lead in under a minute, qualifies them, and books your loan officer, with the compliance layer this industry actually requires. Illustrative lead handling. Yours runs in your own CRM.
  Why does speed to lead decide mortgage conversion?
  Because borrowers shop. A mortgage enquiry usually goes to several lenders at once, and the professional who makes contact first is very often the one who writes the loan. The data is unusually clear here. Harvard and MIT research found 78 percent of buyers close with the first responder, and qualification odds are roughly 21 times higher at five minutes than at thirty. In mortgage specifically, lenders responding within one minute see contact rates above 80 percent, while waiting thirty minutes drops that below 20 percent. The industry target moved, and most teams have not. The familiar five-minute rule is a headline figure; operational mortgage data points to under sixty seconds, because the steepest fall in contact probability happens between the first and second minute. No human team covers that reliably across evenings, weekends and lead spikes. An agent does, and it is doing the mechanical part of the job, contact and qualification, so your loan officer spends their time on people who are actually ready to talk. This is also one of the most heavily litigated verticals in outbound, which is why we build the TCPA-compliant calling layer underneath every deployment rather than selling the dialer alone. See AI voice agents for the general build. Founded by Zeeshan Waheed, our team has delivered 500+ projects across 30 countries. Figures are published industry research, not our client results. - [AI Client Intake for Law Firms](https://imisofts.com/ai-intake-law-firms): Answer and qualify every case enquiry in minutes, day or night. Conflict-aware routing, consent records and calendar booking.

  The Case Goes to Whoever Picks Up. An AI intake agent that answers every case enquiry, screens it against your criteria, captures the facts, and books the consultation, at 2am on a Sunday if that is when they call. Illustrative intake record. Yours runs in your own case system.
  Why does intake speed decide which firm gets the case?
  Because someone with a legal problem is anxious, and anxious people keep calling until a human being responds. The firm that answers is very often the firm that signs them. The gap between best and typical is wide. Top-performing firms respond to online enquiries in under five minutes, while the industry median sits around 13 minutes. Broader research finds 78 percent of buyers close with the first responder, and legal enquiries are no exception. The real problem is not daytime, it is everything else. Accidents, arrests and emergencies do not respect office hours, and a large share of high-value case enquiries arrive at night, at weekends and on holidays. A firm that answers those calls is competing against voicemail. An agent captures the facts while they are fresh, screens against your case criteria so you are not booking consultations you will decline, and books the attorney only when the matter is genuinely in scope. It captures the intake record, flags conflict-check information for a human to review, and hands anything requiring judgement to a person. It never gives legal advice.   Why do real estate leads go cold, and what fixes it?
  Almost always because of the gap between the enquiry arriving and anyone replying to it. Not lead quality, not the portal, not the price of the lead. The gap. The research on this is unusually clear. Harvard Business Review, in work by Oldroyd, McElheran and Elkington, found firms that contacted a web lead within an hour were about seven times more likely to have a meaningful conversation with a decision maker than firms that waited a single hour longer, and more than sixty times more likely than those that waited twenty-four hours. In the same study only 37% of companies managed to reply within an hour at all. Real estate is worse than most sectors, because the enquiry usually arrives while you are already in a showing, and the buyer has sent the same enquiry to three other agents. You cannot beat this with discipline, and you should stop trying. No agent can answer within sixty seconds while showing a property, and the leads that arrive on a Sunday evening are the ones that convert best. The only reliable fix is that the first response does not depend on you being free. An automated SMS and email inside a minute, a qualification exchange that captures timeline, budget and financing, and a booking link that fills your calendar while you are still in the car.   What should an e-commerce brand actually automate first?
  Not the thing most agencies sell you. The largest single pool of recoverable revenue in most stores is not a smarter abandoned cart email, it is the checkout itself. Baymard Institute, averaging fifty separate studies, puts documented cart abandonment at 70.22%. Around 42% of shoppers say they were simply browsing and were never going to buy, which no email will fix. But the rest give reasons that are fixable: 40% left because extra costs were too high, 18% because they were forced to create an account, and 17% because the checkout was too long or complicated. Baymard measures the average US checkout at 23.48 form elements when 12 to 14 is achievable, and estimates the average large store could gain a 35.26% conversion increase from checkout design alone. So we start with the leak, then automate the recovery. Showing shipping cost before the final step and removing forced account creation will usually beat any recovery sequence you can write, because they stop the abandonment happening. Automation then handles what remains: support questions that never needed a human, recovery flows for people who genuinely got distracted, reorder decisions made against a forecast instead of a gut feeling, and pricing that reacts to demand rather than sitting still for a year. ### Free tools

- [Free DNS Propagation Checker (A, CNAME, TXT, MX)](https://imisofts.com/dns-propagation-checker): Check if a new DNS record is live at Google, Cloudflare and four more public DNS providers. A, CNAME, TXT, MX, NS and AAAA, and why a record is not live yet.

  DNS Propagation Checker Added or changed a DNS record? See if it is live at six public DNS providers at once. Add the value you expect, and the checker tells you which providers have it, how long the others keep their old copy, and what to fix if it never shows up. A, CNAME, TXT, MX, NS and AAAA imisofts never sees what you check Asks Google Public DNS, Cloudflare, AliDNS, DNS.SB, Control D and DNS4EU over HTTPS, straight from your browser.
  How to check DNS propagation
  Three fields, one button. The answer comes back in a few seconds. 1 Type the full record name For example test.yourdomain.com, _dmarc.yourdomain.com or yourdomain.com itself, and pick the record type. 2 Add the value you expect The IP address, the CNAME target or the text you saved at your DNS host. It is optional: without it, the checker shows what each provider answers and whether they agree. 3 Read the answer A check mark for every provider that has it, the time left for the ones that do not, and a plain-English note when something will not fix itself.
  What each answer means
  One line per DNS provider, so you can see exactly where your record is and is not live yet.
  Why a DNS change takes time to show up
  DNS propagation is not a push to the whole internet. It is every DNS provider keeping its own copy for a while.
  Cached copies and TTL
  When a DNS provider looks your record up, it keeps the answer for the record's TTL (time to live), as set in RFC 1035. Until that copy expires, it keeps giving out the old value. The TTL it returns counts down, which is how the checker knows the time left at each provider.
  A cached "not found"
  Providers also remember that a name does not exist, for the negative caching time in your zone's SOA record (RFC 2308). Look a name up a minute before you add it, and that provider can keep saying "not found" for that long, often between 5 minutes and an hour.
  The Cloudflare proxy
  When Cloudflare's orange cloud is on, a record answers with Cloudflare's own addresses. That is right for a website, but a tracking domain or a service that needs your real address never shows up. The checker flags it, and waiting will not change it: switch the record to "DNS only".
  Saved at the wr

  How to run a check
  Are your emails landing in spam? Your DNS records could be the reason. Click the checker in your toolbar, type your domain or an email address, and press Check. In seconds, each record gets Pass, Check or Fix, so you know exactly what needs work. Here's what good looks like.
  What good SPF, DKIM, DMARC and MX look like
  SPF: one record, ending in ~all or -all, with ten DNS lookups or fewer. DKIM: a key is found, ideally 2048 bits. Custom selector? Add it here. DMARC: set to quarantine or reject, with a reporting address for daily reports. And MX should point to your email provider's mail servers.
  Fixes and Copy report
  Anything off comes with a plain-English fix and a free guide. Copy report copies it all for whoever runs your DNS. It's free, with no sign-up and no permissions. SPF, DKIM and DMARC Checker, by imisofts.

Anything marked Check or Fix comes with a short How to fix note and a free guide, and Copy report puts the full results on your clipboard for whoever manages your DNS.

  The rules come from the SPF, DKIM and DMARC RFCs and Google's email sender guidelines.

  What is a broken link?
  A broken link points to a page that no longer works. When someone clicks it, the server answers with an error such as 404 Not Found or 410 Gone, a 5xx server error, or no answer at all. Links also break when a domain expires, when a page moves without a redirect, or when a URL is typed wrong.
  Do broken links hurt SEO?
  A 404 on its own does not trigger a penalty. The damage comes from what broken links do to people and crawlers: Visitors hit dead ends. A reader who clicks a broken link often leaves, and a broken link on a service page can cost you a lead. Internal links stop passing value. When a page moves and the links to it are not updated, the new page loses the internal links that help it rank. Crawlers waste time. Search engines spend crawl time on URLs that go nowhere instead of on your live pages.

  Pages you block for crawlers stay out of the sitemap.

  A list of every excluded page and the reason, so you can spot pages that should be indexed.
  What is an XML sitemap?
  An XML sitemap is a file that lists the pages on your site you want search engines to find. It sits at an address such as example.com/sitemap.xml and helps Google and Bing discover new and updated pages faster, especially pages that few other pages link to.
  Do you need a sitemap?
  Search engines can find most pages on a small, well-linked site without one. A sitemap helps most when your site is large, when it is new and has few links from other sites, when pages are hard to reach through your menus, or when you publish often and want new pages found quickly. It never hurts to have one.

  Include pages that load with a 200 status and that you want to appear in search results. Leave out pages marked noindex, URLs that redir

  Free Acronym Generator This acronym generator turns a program, team or project name into short, memorable acronyms. If you already have the letters, enter them and get phrases that fit. Review the result before you publish it
  How to use the Acronym Generator
  Three steps, and results in seconds.

  What makes a good acronym
  A good acronym is short, easy to say and clearly linked to the thing it names. Three to five letters is the usual sweet spot. Longer acronyms are hard to remember, and people end up spelling them out or ignoring them.
  Acronyms and initialisms
  Strictly speaking, an acronym is read as a word, like NASA or SCUBA. An initialism is read letter by letter, like FBI or CEO. Both are useful, but acronyms that form a pronounceable word tend to stick, because people can say them in one breath.
  Two ways to use the generator
  Start with the phrase. Enter the full name, such as "Employee Learning and Mentoring Program", and get short versions built from its key words. Start with the letters. Enter a word you like, such as LEAP or CARE, and get expansions that fit your topic. This is often called a backronym, and it works well for internal programs and campaigns.
  Tips for choosing the final acronym
  Say it out loud. If it sounds awkward or like a different word, people will notice. Search it. Check whether the acronym already means something in your industry. A clash with a well-known term creates confusion. Check the spelled word. Make sure the letters do not form something rude or negative in English or in the languages your audience speaks. Leave small words out. Words like "and", "of" and "the" are usually skipped. Including them makes the acronym longer than it needs to be. Write it out the first time. In documents, give the full name followed by the acronym in brackets, then use the short form after that.

  Acr

  The AI reads the writing style and returns a percentage estimate with the signals it noticed.

  How AI content detection works
  AI writing tools pick likely next words, so their text often has a smooth, predictable pattern. Detectors look for that pattern: sentence lengths that barely vary, safe word choices, stock transitions and paragraphs that summarize instead of saying something specific. This tool asks an AI model to read the text for those signals and explain what it found.
  Why no detector is fully reliable
  Style is not a fingerprint. A careful human writer can produce even, polished prose, and AI text that a person has edited can read as fully human. Results are least reliable when: The text is short. A few sentences do not give enough signal. Aim for several paragraphs. The writer is not a native speaker. Simpler vocabulary and textbook grammar can look machine-like and lead to false flags. The topic is formulaic. Legal notices, product specs and technical instructions follow fixed patterns no matter who writes them. The text was edited or translated. Mixed authorship blurs every signal.
  How to use the estimate responsibly
  Treat it as a prompt for a closer look. Read the signals listed under the score and check them against the text yourself. Never use it as proof. Do not accuse a student, writer or employee based on a detector score. Talk to the person and look at drafts, notes or version history instead. Compare like with like. If you review a writer's work, compare it with earlier pieces you know they wrote.

  Why some text sounds robotic
  Readers notice when writing feels generated or rushed, even if they cannot say why. The usual causes are easy to spot once you know them: Even rhythm. Every sentence has about the same length and shape, so the text drones. Inflated words. "Utilize" instead of "use", "facilitate" instead of "help", "in order to" instead of "to". Stock phrases. Openers like "Since the dawn of time" and closers like "In conclusion, it is clear that" add words without meaning. Vague claims. Statements such as "many experts agree" with no names, numbers or examples. Repetition. The same point made three times in slightly different words.
  What the AI humanizer changes
  The tool rewrites your draft with mixed sentence lengths, plain words and contractions where they fit the voice you pick. It removes filler and cliches and merges repeated points. It keeps your facts, names and numbers, and it keeps the length close to the original, so it does not pad the text or invent examples.
  A quick checklist after you humanize
  Read it aloud. Anything you stumble over needs another edit. Check the facts. Make sure every number, name and claim still matches your source. Add something only you know. A real example, a customer question, a mistake you made. Specific detail is what makes writing feel human. Cut the first sentence. Many drafts warm up before the point. Starting with the second sentence often works better. Match your audience. A LinkedIn post, a client email and a research summary need different voices.

- [Free Grammar Checker: Fix Grammar, Spelling and Punctuation](https://imisofts.com/grammar-checker): Free grammar checker that fixes grammar, spelling and punctuation in one click, then lists the main changes so you can see what went wrong. No sign-up.

  Free Online Grammar Checker Paste your text into this grammar checker to fix grammar, spelling and punctuation without changing your style. You get the clean text first, then a short list of what changed. Review the result before you publish it
  How to use the Grammar Checker
  Three steps, and results in seconds.
  Paste your text
  Add up to 3,500 characters: an email, essay, cover letter, report or social post.
  Choose your spelling
  Keep the text as written, or switch it to American or British spelling.
  Copy the corrected version
  Read the list of changes below the text, then copy the clean version into your document.
  Common grammar mistakes this tool catches
  Homophones: their, there and they're; its and it's; your and you're; affect and effect. Subject and verb agreement: "The list of features are long" should be "The list of features is long", because the subject is "list". Comma splices: two full sentences joined by a comma, such as "We shipped the update, it fixed the bug." Use a period, a semicolon or a joining word. Tense shifts: switching between past and present in the same passage without a reason. Missing articles: "We sent proposal to client" needs "a" or "the". Apostrophes: plurals do not take an apostrophe (one client, two clients), possessives do (the client's invoice).
  How to proofread like an editor
  Take a break first. You miss fewer errors when you come back to a text with fresh eyes. Read it aloud. Missing words and clumsy sentences are easier to hear than to see. Check one thing at a time. Do one pass for names and numbers, then another for punctuation. Read the change list. If the same fix keeps appearing, you have found a habit worth working on.
  American or British spelling
  Pick one variant and use it throughout. The main differences are word endings such as color and colour, organize and organise, center and centre, and some doubled consonants, like traveled and travelled. Leave the setting on Keep as written if your text is in another language or mixes in quoted material.
  What a grammar checker cannot judge
  A checker fixes errors, not ideas. It cannot tell whether your argument is clear, your facts are right or your tone suits the reader. For th

- [Free Conclusion Generator: Write a Strong Closing Paragraph](https://imisofts.com/conclusion-generator): Free conclusion generator for essays, reports and blog posts. Paste your text or main points and get a closing paragraph that sums up and lands. No sign-up.

  Free Conclusion Generator Use this conclusion generator to turn your essay, report or article into a closing paragraph that restates the main point and ends with purpose, without adding new claims. Review the result before you publish it
  How to use the Conclusion Generator
  Three steps, and results in seconds.
  Paste your draft
  Add the full text, or just the thesis and main points if the draft is long.
  Set type and tone
  Choose essay, blog post, report, speech or research paper, then pick a tone.
  Edit the final line
  Check that the conclusion matches your argument and adjust the last sentence so it sounds like you.
  What a good conclusion does
  A conclusion answers the reader's final question: so what? It reminds them of your main point, shows how your evidence fits together and leaves them with something to think about or do next. It should feel like a natural ending, not a copy of your introduction.
  A simple structure that works
  Restate the main idea in new words. One sentence that reflects what the reader now knows. Connect the key points. Show how they add up, rather than listing them again one by one. End with purpose. A wider implication, a recommendation, a call to action or a memorable final line.
  How conclusions differ by type
  Essays and research papers
  Return to your thesis, explain why your findings matter and, where useful, name a limitation or a question for further study. Keep new evidence out of the conclusion.
  Blog posts
  Keep it short. Sum up the takeaway in a sentence or two and tell readers what to do next: try a step, read a related guide or get in touch.
  Reports
  Lead with the decision or recommendation. Busy readers often skip to the end, so the conclusion should stand on its own.
  Speeches
  Repeat the core message, then finish with a line people will remember, such as a callback to your opening story.
  Mistakes to avoid
  Opening with "In conclusion" or "To sum up". The reader can see it is the end. Adding a new argument or statistic that the body never discussed. Apologizing or weakening your claim with phrases like "this is just my opinion". Making it longer than it needs to be. For most essays and posts, one paragraph is enough.

- [Free Emoji Translator: Turn Text Into Emojis and Back](https://imisofts.com/emoji-translator): Free emoji translator: turn text into emojis, add fitting emojis to a message, or decode what a string of emojis means. Pick a mode and copy. No sign-up.

  Free Emoji Translator This emoji translator turns plain text into emojis, adds a few fitting emojis to your message, or decodes an emoji-only text back into words. Review the result before you publish it

  How to use emojis well
  Emojis add tone that plain text lacks. A thumbs up can confirm a plan, and a smile can soften a short reply. Used badly, they confuse or annoy. The emoji translator gives you a starting point, and these tips help you decide what to keep.
  Meanings are not universal
  The same emoji can mean different things to different people. Some carry slang meanings online that have nothing to do with the picture, and gestures that are friendly in one country can be rude in another. If you write to a global audience, stick to clear, literal emojis such as a check mark, a calendar or a light bulb.
  Emojis look different on every device
  Each platform draws its own version of an emoji. A face that looks cheerful on one phone can look awkward on another, and older devices may show a blank box for newer emojis. Keep important meaning in words, and let the emoji support it.
  Think about accessibility
  Screen readers read out the name of every emoji. A line of ten party emojis becomes a long, repeated announcement. A few tips: Use one or two emojis per message or sentence, not long chains. Put emojis at the end of a sentence, not in the middle of words. Never replace key words with emojis in captions or posts that everyone needs to understand.
  Emojis at work
  In team chats, simple reactions are now common and save time. In client emails, proposals and formal documents, it is safer to leave them out unless the client uses them first. On social media, an emoji at the start of a line can work like a bullet point and make a long caption easier to scan.

  When you receive a string of em

  Copy into your design
  Click copy and paste the text into your layout, prototype or template.
  What is lorem ipsum?
  Lorem ipsum is dummy text used to fill a layout before the real words are ready. It looks like Latin, but it is a scrambled version of a passage from De finibus bonorum et malorum, a work on ethics that Cicero wrote in 45 BC. Words were cut, changed and rearranged, so it reads as plausible text with no real meaning.
  Why designers use placeholder text
  It keeps attention on the design. Readable sample copy invites people to edit the words when you want feedback on layout, spacing and type. It has a natural rhythm. The mix of short and long words looks like real text, so line breaks and paragraph shapes are realistic. Everyone recognizes it. No one mistakes lorem ipsum for final copy.
  When to use real copy instead
  Placeholder text hides problems. A headline that fits as two Latin words can break the layout when the real one has twelve. For landing pages, product pages and anything with forms or buttons, draft rough real copy early. The words often change the design: a page may need room for a longer offer, a list of benefits or a price table.
  Tips for working with lorem ipsum
  Match the expected length. If the real product description will be 60 words, use about 60 words of placeholder text, not three paragraphs. Vary paragraph counts. Test a card or blog layout with one short paragraph and with several long ones. Search before you launch. Search your site or code for "lorem" before you publish. Placeholder text on a live page looks unfinished and gives search engines nothing useful to index. Keep it out of alt text and metadata. Fill image descriptions, page titles and meta descriptions with real content from the start, so they are not forg

  Why outline before you write
  An outline is a map of the piece. It shows what each section covers and in what order, before you spend time on sentences. Writers who outline usually finish faster, because they know what comes next, and edit less, because the structure is settled early.
  A basic outline structure
  Introduction: the problem, the question or the thesis, and what the reader will get. Main sections: one idea per section, in an order that builds. Common orders are chronological, problem to solution, simple to advanced, or most to least important. Supporting points: the facts, examples and steps that prove or explain each idea. Conclusion: the takeaway, plus a next step or wider implication.
  Outlining a blog post for search
  If the post needs to rank, start by searching your topic and reading the top results. Note the questions they answer and the gaps they leave. Then: Match the format searchers expect. A "how to" query usually wants steps, while a comparison query wants options side by side. Turn the main sections into clear headings that use the words readers search for. Answer the main question early, then go deeper. Add a section on mistakes, costs or examples if competing pages skip it. That is where you can be more useful.
  Outlining an essay
  Write your thesis as one sentence at the top. Each body section should make one claim that supports it, followed by evidence and a short analysis. If a point does not support the thesis, it belongs in a different essay.

  A generated outline is a first draft of your structure. Cut sections you cannot support with real knowledge or

  The anatomy of a strong paragraph
  A paragraph is one idea, fully explained. Most good paragraphs have three parts: Topic sentence. States the idea. A reader should be able to skim only the first sentences of your paragraphs and still follow the argument. Support. Facts, examples, reasons or steps that explain or prove the idea, in a logical order. Closing sentence. Wraps up the point or links to the next paragraph.
  Example
  Topic sentence: Automating invoices gives a small business back hours every month. Support: Instead of typing each invoice by hand, the accounting system sends them on schedule, fills in the right details and follows up when a payment is late. Close: That time can go into work that brings in revenue instead of chasing it.
  How long should a paragraph be?
  It depends on where it will be read. On websites and in emails, short paragraphs of two to four sentences are easier to scan, especially on phones. Academic and long-form writing allows longer paragraphs, because readers expect to follow a detailed argument. A useful test: if a paragraph covers two ideas, split it.

  When a paragraph needs a rewrite
  Paragraphs usually need work for one of four reasons: the main point is buried in the middle, the sentences do not connect, the paragraph says the same thing twice, or the tone is wrong for the reader. A quick rewrite fixes structure and wording without changing what you mean.
  Five rewriting techniques editors use
  Lead with the point. Move the key sentence to the start. Readers decide in a line or two whether to keep reading. Cut repetition. If two sentences make the same point, keep the stronger one. Swap abstract nouns for verbs. "We made a decision to implement" becomes "We decided to use". Use the active voice. "The report was approved by the board" becomes "The board approved the report". Link the sentences. Each sentence should follow from the one before it. Add a short bridge such as "as a result" only where the connection is not clear.
  Before and after
  Before: There are a number of reasons why it is important for companies to consider the implementation of automation. Automation can save time. It can also reduce errors, and time is saved too. After: Automation helps companies save time and reduce errors. The rewrite is a fraction of the length, leads with the benefit and drops the repeated point, and it adds nothing the original did not say.

- [Free Paraphrasing Tool: Say It Differently, Keep the Meaning](https://imisofts.com/paraphrasing-tool): Free paraphrasing tool that restates your text in new words while keeping the meaning. Choose standard, fluent, formal, simple or shorter mode. No sign-up.

  What paraphrasing is, and what it is not
  To paraphrase is to express the same idea in your own words and sentence structure. A good paraphrase is about as long as the original and keeps every important point. It differs from two related techniques: Summarizing shortens a text to its main points. Quoting copies the exact words inside quotation marks, with credit. Use a paraphrase when the idea matters more than the exact wording, when the original is too technical for your reader, or when you want to fit a source smoothly into your own writing.
  Paraphrasing and plagiarism
  Changing the words does not make an idea yours. In academic work, journalism and professional reports, you still need to cite the source of a paraphrased idea. Paraphrasing your own earlier writing, or text you have rights to, is fine without a citation in most settings. If you are a student, check your institution's rules on AI tools before you use one.
  How to paraphrase well by hand
  Read until you understand. You cannot restate what you have not grasped. Put the source away and write from memory. This forces new wording. Change the structure, not just the words. Start from a different point, or turn a passive sentence into an active one. Keep technical terms. Words like "mortgage" or "API" often have no true synonym, and swapping them can change the meaning. Compare with the original. Check that nothing was lost or added.
  Which mode to choose
  Standard balances new wording and accuracy. Fluent smooths awkward drafts. Formal suits reports and applications. Simple helps you explain co

- [Free Sentence Rewriter: 5 Better Versions of Any Sentence](https://imisofts.com/sentence-rewriter): Free sentence rewriter that gives five fresh versions of any sentence in the style you pick: clearer, shorter, more formal, casual or persuasive. No sign-up.

  Why rewrite one sentence at a time
  Some sentences carry more weight than others: the first line of an email, a headline, the opening of a proposal or the call to action on a page. Small changes there make a big difference, and seeing several versions side by side is the fastest way to find the right one.
  Seven ways to improve a sentence
  Put the subject and verb up front. "After reviewing the numbers from last quarter, our team decided to cut prices" becomes "We cut prices after reviewing last quarter's numbers." Replace weak verb phrases. "Make an improvement" becomes "improve". "Give consideration to" becomes "consider". Cut empty words. Very, really, actually, basically and just rarely add meaning. Remove hedges when you are sure. "We think this might help" becomes "This helps" if you have evidence. Make it concrete. "Solutions that meet your needs" says little. "Payroll software for teams of 5 to 50" says what you do. Use the active voice. "Mistakes were made" hides who made them. "We made a mistake" is honest and clear. Split long sentences. If a sentence has more than one main idea, give each its own sentence.
  Picking the right style
  Clearer for instructions, help content and anything people must act on. Shorter for subject lines, headlines, captions and buttons. More formal for applications, legal or academic writing and first contact with a client. More casual for social posts, newsletters and team chats. More persuasive for sales emails and landing pages, leading with what the reader gains. More confident for proposals and bios where hedging undersells you.

  What makes a good summary
  A good summary lets someone who will never read the original act on it.   Short summary: two or three sentences for a quick update, a link preview or a reply to "what is this about?".   Know the limits
  Summaries lose nuance by design. Caveats, conditions and exceptions are often the first things to go, and they can matter a great deal in contracts, medical information and financial documents.   What alt text is for
  Alt text is the short description in an image's alt attribute. Screen readers read it aloud to people who cannot see the image, browsers show it when an image fails to load, and search engines use it to understand what the image shows. Good alt text serves people first. The search benefits follow.
  How to write good alt text
  Describe what matters on this page. The same photo of a laptop bag needs different alt text on a product page (color, material, style) and on a blog post about remote work (the scene it shows). Keep it short. Aim for about 125 characters or fewer. Long descriptions are tiring to listen to. Skip "image of". Screen readers already announce that it is an image. Include text in the image. If a graphic shows a headline, a price or a quote, put that text in the alt text. Be factual. Describe what is visible. Do not guess who people are or how they feel.
  Examples
  Keyword stuffed: alt="leather bag laptop bag cheap leather laptop bag buy" Useful: alt="Brown leather laptop bag with a brass buckle and padded shoulder strap"
  Decorative images and links
  Images that add nothing to the content, such as background patterns or dividers, should have an empty alt attribute (alt="") so screen readers skip them. If an image is a link or a button, the alt text should say where it goes or what it does, such as "Download the price list".
  Alt text and SEO
  Search engines use alt text, file names and the surrounding text to understand images. Use a keyword only when it accurately describes the image, and never stuff phrases. Descriptive file names, such as brown-leather-

  What a meta description does

  The title tag is the clickable headline of your page in search results and the text shown in browser tabs. It is one of the clearest signals of what a page is about, and it is often the first thing a searcher reads. A clear, specific title helps both search engines and people choose your page.

Repeating variations of a phrase looks spammy and reads badly. Match the page. Google may rewrite titles that do not reflect the content, are too long or are stuffed with keywords.

  Short vertical videos and longer YouTube videos need different pacing. Pick both, plus a tone.
  Read it aloud and record
  Time yourself reading the script, trim lines that feel unnatural, and add your own examples.
  The structure of a video script
  Hook: the first few seconds. State the problem, the promise or a surprising point, so viewers know why to stay. Setup: a line or two of context, such as who this is for or why it matters. Keep it very short in short videos. Main content: the points, steps or story, in a clear order. One idea per point. Call to action: one specific next step. Follow, comment with a question, visit a page or watch the next video.
  How many words do you need?
  Most people speak at roughly 130 to 160 words per minute when they present. That makes a 30-second video about 70 words, a 60-second video about 140 words and a 5-minute video about 700 words. Always read the script aloud with a timer: pauses, demos and on-screen text change the real length.
  Write for the ear, not the eye
  Use short sentences and everyday words. If a line is hard to say, rewrite it. Say numbers simply: "about half" is easier to follow than "48.7 percent". Repeat the key point near the end. Viewers cannot scroll back up the way readers can. Write cues for what appears on screen, so filming and editing go faster.
  Short videos versus longer videos
  For Reels, TikTok and Shorts, cover one idea, open with the payoff and cut every line that does not move the video forward. Add on-screen text, because many people watch with the sound off. For YouTube videos of several minutes, a brief intro that previews what is coming helps viewers decide to stay, and chapters make long videos easier to navigate.
  Make the script yours
  A script is a starting point.

Essay hooks can be a question, a striking fact you can source or a short scene.
  Deliver on the promise
  A hook is a promise. If the content does not pay it off, people leave and trust you less next time. Write the content first, then choose the hook that sums up its mo

A descriptive name, such as "Budget Travel Asia", tells viewers what to expect. An invented or personal name needs strong thumbnails and titles to explain itself. Room to grow. "Lina Travels" can cover any destination. "Lina in Bali" is stuck if you move on. Timeless. Avoid years, ages and trends that will date the channel. Distinct. A name close to a big channel confuses viewers and can cause problems if it looks like impersonation.
  Four naming approaches
  Personal brand: your name, or your name plus a niche word. Ideal if you are the face of the channel. Descriptive: says the topic directly. Good for search and for faceless channels. Compound: two words combined, like "DeskLab" or "BudgetBackpack". Abstract: a memorable word with no obvious meaning. Distinctive, but it takes more effort to build.
  Before you choose
  Search the name on YouTube and in a web search, check whether the handle and the same name on other social platforms are free, and say it aloud

  Slogan or tagline?
  The words are often used interchangeably. In practice, a tagline is a lasting line tied to the brand itself, used next to the logo for years. A slogan often belongs to a campaign or product and may change more often. Both need to be short, clear and easy to remember.
  What makes a slogan stick
  Brevity. Short lines are easier to remember, so aim for under eight words. One idea. A slogan that tries to say three things says nothing. A benefit or feeling. What the customer gets or how they feel, not a list of features. Sound. Rhythm, rhyme and repeated sounds make lines easier to recall. Fit. A playful line suits a bakery. A calm, confident one suits a law firm.

  Plain promise: say the benefit directly. "Fresh bread before sunrise." Alliteration: repeat a first sound. "Simply soft sourdough." "Wake up to real bread."

  Generic phrases any company could use, such as "quality you can trust". Claims you cannot support, like being the cheapest or the first. These can mislead customers and break advertising rules. Lines that depend on a pun only a few people will get. Copying the structure of a famous slogan too closely.
