## Cold email, cold calling and data law guides

Plain-language guides to the anti-spam, calling and data rules that apply to B2B outreach: one page per country for cold email (46 countries), plus cold calling, AI caller disclosure, list buying and web scraping. Each states the governing statute, the consent basis for business-to-business contact, identification and unsubscribe duties, the regulator and the penalties.

- [AI Caller Disclosure Laws by State: What Actually Binds a Business](https://imisofts.com/blog/ai-caller-disclosure-laws-by-state/): September 5, 2026. Ask a compliance vendor which US states require an AI caller to announce itself and you will get a list that includes Colorado, effective June 30, 2026. Colorado's general disclosure duty is still printed in the statute with that date, but the legislature repealed and replaced the whole law in May 2026 with a version that contains no such duty from January 1, 2027, and a federal court order from April 2026 bars the Attorney General from even opening an investigation under either version. Most 2025 guides have not caught up. The wider truth, read from the statutes rather than the summaries, is that as of today no federal rule and no state law requires an ordinary private business to proactively announce "this is an AI" on a consented live sales call. What binds AI voice deployments is narrower, older and mostly about consent. Here is the map.
- [Call Recording Laws by State: One-Party vs All-Party Consent](https://imisofts.com/blog/call-recording-laws-by-state/): October 15, 2026. By the count of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, 13 US states require the consent of everyone on a phone call before it is recorded: California, Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Montana, Nevada, New Hampshire, Pennsylvania and Washington, with Michigan's rule confirmed at least for recordings by someone outside the conversation. Federal law and the other states need only one party's consent, and Vermont has no state law at all. In California a recording made without the required consent can cost $5,000 per violation in a civil suit. For any business that records calls, and especially one using an AI receptionist or an AI notetaker, the safe default is a clear recording notice at the start of every call.
- [Cold Calling Laws in Australia: Do Not Call Register, Hours and AI Voices](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-calling-laws-australia/): September 29, 2026. Cold calling is legal in Australia. Two instruments decide who you may call and how: the Do Not Call Register Act 2006, which bars telemarketing calls to registered numbers unless the account-holder consented, and the Telecommunications (Telemarketing and Research Calls) Industry Standard 2017, which sets calling hours, identification, caller ID and hang-up rules for every telemarketing call, calls to businesses included. An AI voice agent is caught by both, because the Act defines a voice call to include "a call that involves a recorded or synthetic voice". Since July 1, 2026 a Commonwealth penalty unit is worth A$364, so the court maximum for a first-time company is A$36,400 per call to a registered number and A$728,000 for all such calls on one day. The Standard itself is due to sunset on April 1, 2027.
- [Cold Calling Laws in Belgium: Opt-Out Today, Opt-In Bill Pending](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-calling-laws-belgium/): November 2, 2026. Belgium is still an opt-out country for live sales calls, and a bill to change that was filed in the federal parliament with a critical opinion from the data protection authority attached. Under Book VI of the Code de droit économique, a live call for direct marketing is allowed "en l'absence d'opposition manifeste du destinataire, personne physique ou morale," unless the number is on the "Ne m'appelez plus" list, the Do Not Call Me register that the FPS Economy says makes "Tout appel publicitaire vers un numéro de téléphone qui figure dans ce fichier" illegal. Automated calls without a human and faxes need prior consent.
- [Cold Calling Laws by Country (2026): B2B, AI Voices and Fines](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-calling-laws-by-country/): October 11, 2026. Cold calling a business is legal in most of the big English-speaking and Gulf markets, but the rules differ on the three things that decide a program: whether a business number needs consent, which hours you may call, and whether an AI or recorded voice changes the answer. In six of the nine countries below you may make a live call to a business without its consent. Germany asks for at least presumed consent, Austria for prior consent, and South Africa's regulator reads its data protection law as allowing one call to a non-customer, only to ask for consent. An AI voice needs consent or approval in most of the markets in this table. Penalties include up to $1,500 per violation in US private lawsuits and up to 17.5 million pounds or 4 percent of worldwide turnover in the UK.
- [Cold Calling Laws in Canada: DNCL, Calling Hours and AI Voices](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-calling-laws-canada/): October 11, 2026. Cold calling a Canadian business is legal, and it skips the National Do Not Call List: the CRTC's rules say the list rules "do not apply to a telemarketing telecommunication made to a business consumer." Everything else still applies. The Telemarketing Rules, which cover registration, calling hours from 9:00 a.m. to 9:30 p.m. on weekdays, caller ID and your own do not call list, apply "whether or not the telemarketing telecommunication is exempt" from the list, and so do the rules for automatic dialing-announcing devices, whose wording reaches AI voice agents. Each breach can cost a company up to $15,000, and on October 7, 2026 the CRTC set a $10,000 penalty for a sole proprietor trading as Window Brothers whose notice of violation listed 202 breaches.
- [Cold Calling Laws in Germany and Austria: The AI Voice Agent Rules](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-calling-laws-germany-austria/): October 6, 2026. Germany and Austria split on the question every outbound team asks first: may we call a business that has never heard of us? In Germany a human caller may, on the business's presumed consent, but advertising with an automatic calling machine needs the addressee's prior express consent whoever the addressee is, and an AI voice agent that dials and talks with no person on the line fits that description on a plain reading. Austria needs prior consent for every advertising call, businesses included. The fines are real: the Bundesnetzagentur can fine an advertising call to a consumer without consent up to €300,000 under section 20 of the German Unfair Competition Act (UWG), and Austria's Telecommunications Act 2021 allows up to €100,000 for an advertising call made without consent.
- [Cold Calling Laws in India: TRAI's 2026 Rules for AI Calls](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-calling-laws-india/): October 26, 2026. Cold calling is legal in India only inside the registration system the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) requires, and from about 17 November 2026 that system also requires AI callers to be declared in advance. Under the Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026, which TRAI announced on 18 September 2026, any voice call that software places without a person dialing it, whether an autodialer, a robocall or an AI voice agent, is an Application-to-Person (A2P) call. Every business that makes A2P calls must declare them to its telecom operator in advance, with the numbers it will use, and an undeclared A2P call is treated as unsolicited commercial communication, the regulator's term for spam. Promotional calls already belong on 140-series numbers.
- [Cold Calling Laws in Ireland: Mobiles Need Consent First](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-calling-laws-ireland/): November 2, 2026. In Ireland a sales call to a mobile phone needs the person's prior consent, and the text of the rule is not limited to private individuals, so we read it as covering business mobiles too. A sales call to a landline is allowed unless the line is on the National Directory Database (NDD) opt-out register or the person has told you no. On our reading, an AI voice agent that dials and talks with no human involved is an automated calling machine, which needs prior consent before it calls an individual. Every unlawful call is a separate criminal offence, punishable by up to €5,000 on summary conviction and up to €250,000 for a company convicted on indictment. Statute and regulator texts read on 2 November 2026: S.I. 336/2011 as made and the Fines Act 2010 on irishstatutebook.ie, DPC releases on dataprotection.ie, comreg.ie and EUR-Lex.
- [Cold Calling Laws in Italy: RPO Register, 15-Day Scrubs, TIM Fine](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-calling-laws-italy/): November 2, 2026. In Italy a cold call can be blocked before it rings and fined after it does. Since 27 July 2022 the Registro pubblico delle opposizioni, the public opt-out register, has covered every national fixed and mobile number, listed or not, and registration cancels any marketing consent the person gave before, except to companies they hold a contract with. An operator must register with the RPO, buy an annual subscription priced by list size, from 68 euro for 10,000 numbers to 43,040 euro for 10 million (band 45 of 60-plus), and check its lists "mensilmente, e comunque precedentemente all'inizio di ogni campagna promozionale": monthly and before every campaign, with each check valid for only 15 days.
- [Cold Calling Laws in the Netherlands (2026): Bel-me-niet to Opt-In](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-calling-laws-netherlands/): October 15, 2026. Since 1 July 2026, a company may phone a Dutch consumer, sole proprietor, vof or maatschap to sell something only if that person gave explicit prior consent. Being a current or former customer no longer counts, except for charities, charity lotteries and newspaper and magazine publishers. The Bel-me-niet Register, the do-not-call list many guides still mention, closed on 1 July 2021, when the Netherlands switched to opt-in. Live calls to companies with legal personality, such as a BV or NV, sit outside the consent rule for calls, but automated calls need prior consent from businesses as well as consumers, subject to narrow exceptions, which matters for anyone planning AI voice agents for Dutch outbound.
- [Cold Calling Laws in New Zealand: Code Hours, 5 Working Days](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-calling-laws-new-zealand/): November 2, 2026. New Zealand has no national do-not-call register in law and no statute that fixes the hours of a live sales call. Three sources matter: one binding statute, one industry code, and a spam law that stops at voice calls. The Fair Trading Act 1986 treats any sale over $100 negotiated on a call the consumer did not invite as an "uninvited direct sale agreement": it must be in writing, a copy must reach the consumer within 5 working days, the consumer must be told orally of a 5 working day right to cancel before agreeing, and a supplier that skips those steps cannot enforce the contract and can be fined up to $10,000 as an individual or $30,000 as a company.
- [Cold Calling Laws in Pakistan: PTA Rules and the 3627 Register](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-calling-laws-pakistan/): November 2, 2026. Pakistan regulates sales calls through the PTA's spam regulations of 2009, as amended in 2020 and again by a second amendment in force from its Gazette publication on 31 December 2022. That amendment defines a telemarketer as a person authorized by the PTA, requires operators to ensure telemarketers are registered, and treats marketing to people who have not consented and are on the central Do Not Call Register, which subscribers join through the short code 3627, as unsolicited. Operators may carry robocalls only for public awareness. On our reading, PECA's spam offence can also reach a sales call: unsolicited spam is fined up to Rs 50,000 the first time and up to Rs 1,000,000 for each later violation. PTA regulations (2009, 2020 and 2022 Gazette texts on pta.gov.pk) and PECA 2016 as consolidated to 2025, read on 2 November 2026.
- [Cold Calling Laws in Poland: Consent Before the First Call (2026)](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-calling-laws-poland/): October 15, 2026. In Poland, a sales call needs the recipient's consent before the phone rings. Article 398 of the Electronic Communications Law, in force since 10 November 2024, bans using telecommunications terminal equipment or automated calling systems for direct marketing to any subscriber or end user who has not agreed in advance, and the law's definition of an end user covers companies too. In a decision announced on 3 September 2026, the consumer authority, UOKiK, fined a telemarketing firm PLN 308,728 and its president at the time PLN 100,000 for calling consumers without consent, rejecting the firm's defense that its agents "only" booked meetings. For anyone planning AI voice agents or a call team for the Polish market, this guide covers what the law requires and how the regulators read it.
- [Cold Calling Laws in South Africa: Your AI Agent Gets One Call](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-calling-laws-south-africa/): South African law lets an AI voice agent cold call a business that is not your customer at most once, and only to ask for consent. POPIA names automatic calling machines in section 69 and protects companies as well as people, and the Information Regulator’s guidance says that one call must carry the contents of Form 4 and record the answer. The opt-out registry whose rules were gazetted on 15 April 2026 sits on top of that rule, not in place of it. One search about POPIA, B2B cold calling and juristic persons showed my site 1,615 times in 28 days of Search Console data and earned no click. On 5 October 2026 I read the Act in the Government Gazette, the Regulator’s Guidance Note on Direct Marketing and the National Consumer Commission’s draft registry guidelines of 2 October.
- [Cold Calling Laws in Spain: Sales Calls Now Need a 400 Number](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-calling-laws-spain/): October 26, 2026. Since 17 October 2026, sales calls in Spain must come from a nine-digit number starting with 400, and operators must block numbers that show signs of commercial calling without that code. The rule sits on top of the consent rule in force since 29 June 2023: a sales call needs prior consent or another legal basis under the GDPR, which the data protection authority (AEPD) reads narrowly, and an automated commercial call with no human on the line needs prior consent in every case. That second rule is the one an AI voice agent meets. A serious breach can cost up to €2 million. Statute and regulator texts read on 26 October 2026 in the BOE (Resolution of 14 April 2026, Law 10/2025, Law 11/2022, AEPD Circular 1/2023), on aepd.es and on EUR-Lex.
- [Cold Calling Laws in Sweden: NIX, Written Acceptance, Ban Inquiry](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-calling-laws-sweden/): November 2, 2026. Sweden lets a company cold call a private person unless that person has said no, and it is now asking whether to reverse the rule. On 9 July 2026 the government announced an inquiry into telephone sales that will examine an opt-in requirement and a possible ban, with a report due by 15 January 2027. These are the rules today. Under section 21 of the Marknadsföringslag, a trader may use live calls to a natural person "om inte den fysiska personen tydligt motsatt sig att metoden används," and the practical form of that objection is the industry register NIX-Telefon, which NIX-Telefon says marketers must, with certain exceptions, check before calling. Automated calls, email and fax to a natural person need prior consent under section 19.
- [Cold Calling Laws in Switzerland: Star Entries and Caller ID](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-calling-laws-switzerland/): November 2, 2026. Switzerland allows cold calls by default and then puts starred and unlisted numbers off limits to advertising callers with no business relationship. Under article 3, paragraph 1, letter u of the Bundesgesetz gegen den unlauteren Wettbewerb (UWG), the federal unfair competition act, it is unfair to ignore a star (*) next to a person's telephone directory entry, and anyone with no directory entry at all is treated as if they had the star. The State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) puts the rule plainly on its page about unwanted advertising calls: "Telefonmarketing ist in der Schweiz grundsätzlich erlaubt," telemarketing is allowed in principle, but for a starred or unlisted number "ist eine telefonische Kontaktaufnahme zu Werbezwecken unzulässig." Since 1 January 2021, letter v adds that an advertising call must display a number that is listed in the directory...
- [Cold Calling Laws in the UAE: Can an AI Voice Agent Make the Call?](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-calling-laws-uae/): Yes. Cabinet Resolution No. 56 of 2024, the UAE’s telemarketing rules in force since 27 August 2024, says automated communication systems may be used for marketing. The agent then carries every duty a human caller has: a licensed UAE company with prior approval, numbers registered to its own trade licence, calls only from 9:00 am to 6:00 pm, nobody on the Do Not Call Registry, and an opening that names the company, the purpose and the recording, then asks to continue. Resolution No. 57 fines a company AED 10,000 to AED 150,000 per breach. I run imisofts from Dubai, and I read both resolutions on the UAE legislation portal on 30 September 2026. The robot is the settled part. The fines sit in everything attached to it, starting with the number your agent dials from.
- [Cold Calling Laws in the UK: CTPS, AI Voices and the New Fine Ceiling](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-calling-laws-uk/): September 5, 2026. Cold calling a UK business is legal. Cold calling it with an AI voice is, on the regulator's own enforcement record, not legal without that business's prior consent. That distinction decides more outbound strategy than the whole of the rest of the rulebook, and it comes from three cases decided in 2025 and 2026 in which the Information Commissioner treated calls where a human agent played pre-recorded clips in reply to the recipient as automated calls needing consent. Since February 5, 2026 the ceiling for those breaches is 17.5 million pounds or 4 percent of worldwide turnover, and every unanswered dialler attempt now counts as a call. Here is the UK regime for live calls, automated calls and AI voices, from the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations, the ICO and Ofcom.
- [Cold Email Laws in Argentina: Allowed Without Consent, If You Label It](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-argentina/): October 5, 2026. Argentina has no prior-consent rule for advertising email. It has a source, labelling and removal rule instead. Article 27 of Law 25.326 on personal data protection lets a business process data for advertising and direct sales when the data appear in publicly accessible documents, were provided by the people themselves or were obtained with their consent, and lets every person ask at any time to be withdrawn or blocked from the database. Decree 1558/2001 requires every advertising communication sent by mail, telephone, email or other remote means to state expressly and prominently that the recipient can ask for that removal, and Disposition 4/2009 of March 4, 2009 adds that unsolicited direct advertising must be flagged as advertising, with the single word "publicidad" in the header of an email.
- [Cold Email Laws in Australia: Spam Act Guide (2026)](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-australia/): Cold email in Australia is legal for B2B outreach under the Spam Act 2003, provided you have inferred consent or actual consent. The key advantage is that inferred consent, derived from published business email addresses, is recognized by Australia's ACMA (Australian Communications and Media Authority). Unlike Canada's strict CASL requirements, Australia takes a practical approach: if someone publishes a business email, they've implicitly consented to business contact. We've successfully expanded to Australian markets using this framework, maintaining 70-85% inbox placement rates and low complaint rates across our outreach campaigns. The Spam Act is Australia's primary anti-spam law, enforced by the ACMA. It applies to all commercial electronic messages sent by or to Australian recipients. The Act is somewhat less stringent than Canada's CASL or GDPR, but more complex than US CAN-SPAM.
- [Cold Email Laws in Austria: A Three-Email Sequence Has a Price](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-austria/): September 5, 2026. Austria is the one country where the standard three-email cold sequence has literally been tried in court and priced. In December 2024 the Federal Administrative Court upheld fines against a video marketing agency owner for a three-step sequence sent to a company managing director: 600 euro for the first email, 600 for the second, and 800 for the "just checking one last time" follow-up, which was treated as intentional because it went out after the authority had already asked him to explain the first two. Austria's rule is opt-in for everyone, business recipients included, the courts read consent to the GDPR standard, and the famous Austrian "Robinson list" is misunderstood twice over. Here is the law as it stands in the Telecommunications Act 2021 and how it has been applied.
- [Cold Email Laws in Belgium: The info@ Exception Has a Catch](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-belgium/): September 5, 2026. Belgium appears on most "B2B cold email is fine here" lists because its law contains a genuine exception for emailing companies. The exception is real. It is also narrower than the lists say, the regulator has declined to apply it in the one recent case that looked like ordinary B2B prospecting, and since February 1, 2026 the criminal fine attached to the underlying ban is multiplied by ten. This is what the Code of Economic Law, the 2003 Royal Decree and the Data Protection Authority actually say. Article XII.13, section 1, of the Code de droit économique prohibits the use of electronic mail for advertising without the recipient's prior, free, specific and informed consent. Section 4 puts the burden of proving that the advertising was solicited on the sender.
- [Cold Email Laws in Brazil: The First LGPD Fine Was a List](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-brazil/): September 17, 2026. Brazil looks hard on paper. The LGPD is modelled on the GDPR, fines reach R$50 million, and most write ups tell you to collect consent first. The statute does not say that, and the enforcement record points somewhere more specific: Brazil's first ever LGPD fine was issued over a contact list. The words spam, e-mail and marketing appear zero times in the LGPD, zero times in the Marco Civil da Internet and zero times in the Consumer Defence Code. Decreto 11.034/2022 governs inbound customer service and says expressly that it does not apply to the offer of products and services.
- [Cold Email Laws in Bulgaria: The KZP Opt-Out Register for Companies](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-bulgaria/): October 27, 2026. Bulgaria lets you send unsolicited commercial email to companies without their prior consent, but not to any address a company has entered in the opt-out register run by the Commission for Consumer Protection (KZP), and not to consumers at all without prior consent. Every unsolicited message must be recognisable as unsolicited the moment it arrives. KZP's online checker compares up to 100,000 addresses per request against the register. Breaches cost 250 to 1,500 leva for a person and 500 to 2,000 leva for a company, about EUR 128 to EUR 767 and EUR 256 to EUR 1,023 at the 1.95583 rate that has applied since Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 January 2026.
- [Cold Email Laws by Country: The 31-Country Comparison Table (2026)](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-by-country/): September 27, 2026. Cold email to a business contact needs prior consent in 13 of the 31 countries covered in this table, is allowed on the strength of a conspicuously published business address in 4, is allowed to businesses without prior consent in 8 provided the sender is identified and opt-outs are honoured, and sits under general data protection or consumer law rather than an anti-spam statute in the remaining 6. Those four groups, not "GDPR or not", are the split that decides whether a sequence is lawful. Every row below links to the full country guide, which quotes the statute, the regulator's own guidance and the published cases. Statutes and regulator pages read from 26 to 28 September 2026; the linked country guides cite each provision.
- [Cold Email Laws in Canada: CASL Compliance Guide (2026)](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-canada/): Canada has the strictest email law in the world, the Canadian Anti-Spam Law (CASL). Unlike the US (CAN-SPAM opt-out) or UK (PECR soft opt-in), Canada requires prior consent before sending any commercial email, including B2B. However, a loophole exists for B2B: implied consent is valid for B2B emails to business addresses when you can demonstrate the contact information was published (e.g., on a company website or LinkedIn). We've successfully operated in Canada by leveraging this implied consent rule, reaching 26,500+ decision-makers across 30+ countries, including Canadian prospects with 70-85% inbox placement rates. CASL came into force on July 1, 2014, and is enforced by the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC), Competition Bureau, and Privacy Commissioner.
- [Cold Email Laws in Colombia: Ley 1581, Consent and Sending Hours](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-colombia/): October 11, 2026. Colombia treats a cold email to a named person as processing of personal data, and its data protection law requires the person's authorization, which it defines as "consentimiento previo, expreso e informado", prior, express and informed consent, before you process it. A second law, Ley 2300 de 2023, limits advertising emails to consumers to Monday to Friday from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. and Saturday from 8:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m., with nothing on Sundays or public holidays. The regulator, the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC), can fine a company up to 2,000 monthly minimum wages per sanction, and in October 2025 it announced a COP 670 million sanction against Movistar for commercial contact without authorization.
- [Cold Email Laws in the Czech Republic: Opt-In for Companies Too](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-czech-republic/): October 15, 2026. In the Czech Republic, a business may send commercial email only to people who agreed to it in advance or to its own customers about similar products, and the rule makes no distinction between individuals and companies. The Office for Personal Data Protection (ÚOOÚ), which enforces it, says contact details found on the internet cannot be used, that a purchased database of business contacts is practically unusable, and that an email asking for consent is itself a commercial message. A business that sends unsolicited commercial email in bulk or repeatedly faces fines of up to CZK 10 million. We build cold email infrastructure for B2B teams, so this guide explains what Czech law allows and how a compliant campaign has to work. The rules come from the current text of Act No. 480/2004 Coll.
- [Cold Email Laws in Denmark: Every Sending Domain Is a Separate Fine](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-denmark/): September 5, 2026. Denmark's spam rule is one sentence long and it contains no exception for business recipients: a trader may not contact anyone by email for direct marketing without prior consent. The Consumer Ombudsman's guidance says the word "anyone" means consumers, companies and public authorities alike, and that it makes no difference whether the address is info@company.dk or the managing director's personal mailbox. What most write-ups miss is how the fines are counted. The prosecution service's tariff treats each campaign and each sender identity as a separate count with its own minimum, which means the standard cold-email setup of one campaign across ten rotating domains is priced as ten offences before a single reply arrives. The current consolidation is Act No. 1420 of 2 December 2024.
- [Cold Email Laws in Finland: Work Emails Need Consent or a Role Match](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-finland/): October 27, 2026. Finland is not the opt-out B2B market that many cold email guides describe. Section 200 of the Act on Electronic Communications Services (917/2014), the law formerly called the Information Society Code, allows email marketing to natural persons only with their prior consent, and Finland's Data Protection Ombudsman treats an address like firstname.lastname@company.fi as belonging to a natural person. The exception is what the Ombudsman calls authorisation by role: no consent is needed when the recipient's job is essentially linked to what you sell, and you must check and document that before the first send. Mail to a company's general address, such as info@, needs no consent but must honour an opt-out.
- [Cold Email Laws in France: CNIL & GDPR Guide (2026)](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-france/): Cold email in France is governed by GDPR (EU-wide) and specific guidance from CNIL, France's data protection authority. Unlike some EU countries, France allows legitimate interest for B2B cold email, meaning you can send unsolicited emails to professional business addresses without explicit prior consent, provided you have a documented legitimate business interest. However, B2C cold email to consumers requires explicit opt-in consent. As of August 2026, France is tightening B2C consent requirements, making compliance even more critical. We've successfully expanded across Europe, including France, maintaining 70-85% inbox placement by leveraging legitimate interest for B2B outreach while respecting the upcoming B2C consent mandate.
- [Cold Email Laws in Germany: UWG & GDPR Guide (2026)](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-germany/): Germany has the strictest cold email regulations in Europe. The Unfair Competition Act (UWG Section 7) bans unsolicited cold emails to businesses without prior consent or legitimate interest. GDPR adds another layer. But B2B cold email isn't dead in Germany, it's just heavily regulated. We've run 50+ campaigns in Germany using .de domains and German personas. Reply rates hit 5-8% when compliance is tight. Here's exactly what you need to know.
- [Cold Email Laws in Greece: Opt-In Even for Companies](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-greece/): November 2, 2026. Greece is an opt-in country for marketing email with one twist that catches business-to-business senders: the rule applies to companies as well as people. Article 11 of Law 3471/2006 allows unsolicited electronic communications for direct marketing "μόνο αν ο συνδρομητής συγκατατεθεί εκ των προτέρων ρητώς," only if the subscriber has consented in advance and expressly, and paragraph 7 states that "Οι ανωτέρω ρυθμίσεις ισχύουν και για τους συνδρομητές που είναι νομικά πρόσωπα," the rules also apply to subscribers that are legal persons. The only exception is the soft opt-in for existing customers of similar products, with a free and easy objection route in every message. Every marketing email must identify the sender and give a valid address for stopping the messages, and under Presidential Decree 131/2003 the subject line must flag the commercial nature of the content.
- [Cold Email Laws in Hong Kong: What the UEMO and PDPO Require](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-hong-kong/): September 8, 2026. Hong Kong is one of the few markets where cold email is lawful without prior consent, and where the contact record you used to send it is governed by a criminal statute carrying a HK$500,000 fine and three years in prison. Both things are true at once. Most compliance guides pick one and ignore the other, which is why so many outbound teams either avoid Hong Kong entirely or walk into it assuming an opt-out market means no rules at all. The rules sit in two ordinances enforced by two different regulators. Get the split right and Hong Kong is one of the more workable Tier-1 Asian markets for B2B outbound. Get it wrong and the exposure is not the email you sent, it is the list you bought.
- [Cold Email Laws in India: IT Act & Email Regulations (2026)](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-india/): India's B2B market is growing faster than anywhere else. But cold email compliance is confusing. The Information Technology Act (IT Act) Section 5, combined with DND registry rules and IAMAI guidelines, creates a complex legal landscape. The good news: B2B cold email is mostly legal in India. The tricky part: enforcement varies by state. - [Cold Email Laws in Indonesia: The PDP Law, PP 33/2026 and a Regulator That Does Not Exist Yet](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-indonesia/): September 28, 2026. Indonesia has no anti-spam statute for email. What it has, since October 17, 2022, is Law No. 27 of 2022 on Personal Data Protection, the PDP Law, modelled closely on the EU's GDPR, and since October 17, 2024 the two-year transition period is over and every provision is enforceable. For cold email that produces a familiar shape: a named person's work address is personal data, sending to it is processing, and the sender needs one of six lawful bases and must honour the right to withdraw and object. Two things changed this summer. On July 16, 2026 the government promulgated Government Regulation No. 33 of 2026, the PDP Law's implementing regulation, which takes effect on January 16, 2027 and spells out how consent is asked for, proved and withdrawn.
- [Cold Email Laws in Ireland: Per-Email Fines, But Warned First](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-ireland/): September 5, 2026. Ireland is the last large English-speaking market most outbound teams add to a sequence without checking the rules, on the theory that an EU country with a Data Protection Commission in Dublin must simply be "GDPR, so no." The actual law is narrower and stranger than that. The statute puts the burden of proving consent on the sender, treats every email as a separate offence, and allows a fine of up to 250,000 euro on indictment. Yet the largest penalty the DPC has ever published for marketing offences is 6,000 euro, and in 2025 it closed 275 investigations, sent 50 warning letters and prosecuted nobody. Then on 7 September 2026 it went back to court and won. Here is what the regulation actually says, what the regulator actually does, and what a business sending to Irish inboxes should do about the gap. Ireland implemented the ePrivacy Directive through S.I. No.
- [Cold Email Laws in Israel: Opt-In, Section 30A and ILS 1,000 Damages](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-israel/): October 11, 2026. Israel is one of the strictest countries in the world for cold email. Section 30A of the Communications Law, Israel's anti-spam law, bans advertising by email without the recipient's prior, explicit consent in writing, allows a single message to a business asking for that consent, and lets a court award up to ILS 1,000 for every advertising email received in breach, without the recipient having to prove any harm. A sender is presumed to have acted knowingly unless it proves otherwise, and every advertising email must carry the Hebrew word for advertisement in its subject line. This guide reads section 30A in the Hebrew text of the Communications Law (Telecommunications and Broadcasting), 5742-1982, as published on Wikisource, read 11 October 2026; the translations are ours.
- [Cold Email Laws in Italy: Article 130 and the Garante (2026)](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-italy/): Cold email into Italy needs the recipient's prior consent. That rule is Article 130 of the Italian Privacy Code, legislative decree 196/2003, and since 2012 it has covered companies as well as individuals. There is no business-to-business carve-out and no legitimate interest route around it. The surprise is what Italy allows instead. A live operator call to a number in a public directory that is not on the national opposition register is permitted, and the Italian regulator has said in writing that you may make that call specifically to ask for consent to email. Italy is one of the few places in Europe where the phone is the permissive channel and the inbox is the restricted one.
- [Cold Email Laws in Japan: Opt-In, With One B2B Exception That Still Works](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-japan/): September 22, 2026. Cold email to Japan is legal, and it is opt-in. Japan switched from an opt-out regime to an opt-in regime in 2008, so the default is that you may not send advertising email to a Japanese recipient without consent. The reason outbound teams still run Japan sequences is a fourth exception written into the statute itself: an organization, or an individual engaged in business, who has disclosed their own email address. That carve-out is what makes B2B prospecting into Japan workable, and it is narrower than most sales teams assume. The governing statute is the Act on Regulation of Transmission of Specified Electronic Mail, Act No. 26 of 17 April 2002, amended by Act No. 54 of 6 June 2008.
- [Cold Email Laws in Malaysia: PDPA Consent and the Coming Spam Rule](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-malaysia/): October 11, 2026. As far as we could find, Malaysia has no anti-spam rule for email in operation yet, but cold email to a named person is still regulated. The Personal Data Protection Act 2010 requires consent to process personal data in commercial transactions, requires a written notice explaining what you do with it, and gives everyone the right to stop direct marketing at any time. Since April 1, 2025, breaching those principles can cost up to RM1,000,000, up to three years in prison, or both. A new section 233A of the Communications and Multimedia Act, which bans unsolicited commercial electronic messages, has been enacted but was not yet in operation when the regulator consulted on the rules that would implement it.
- [Cold Email Laws in Mexico: Your Email Has to Name the Regulator](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-mexico/): September 21, 2026. Every guide to cold email in Mexico points at the same statute, the Ley Federal de Proteccion de Datos Personales en Posesion de los Particulares, and then explains consent. Read the law and the advice falls apart. The current LFPDPPP does not contain the word marketing, the word advertising, or the words electronic mail. The rule that actually governs a marketing email to somebody in Mexico lives in a different statute, enforced by a different regulator, and it requires something no other market we have covered requires: your email has to print the regulator's own contact details. We read the consolidated LFPDPPP published by the Camara de Diputados, last reformed in the Diario Oficial de la Federacion on 14 November 2025. The terms mercadotecnia, publicidad, publicitaria, prospeccion comercial and correo electronico appear zero times in it.
- [Cold Email Laws in the Netherlands: Article 11.7 and the GDPR (2026)](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-netherlands/): Cold email to a recipient in the Netherlands is prohibited unless you can prove the recipient agreed to receive it beforehand, and that is true for businesses as well as consumers. The rule is Article 11.7 of the Telecommunicatiewet, the Dutch telecommunications act, and it opens with the burden of proof already assigned: unsolicited commercial electronic messages are banned "unless the sender can demonstrate" prior consent. The regulator, the Authority for Consumers and Markets (ACM), tells senders to be able to prove that consent up to five years after a message goes out. There are two escape routes for B2B senders, and both are narrower than most English-language guides suggest: an address the recipient itself published for the purpose of receiving offers, and your own existing customers.
- [Cold Email Laws New Zealand: A .nz Address Is Enough](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-new-zealand/): Almost every cold email guide tells you New Zealand's spam law only reaches New Zealand senders. That is the wrong section, and it is why people put .nz addresses back into their sequencer with a clear conscience. Here is the plain answer. The Unsolicited Electronic Messages Act 2007 tests the message, not the sender. Under section 4(2)(f), an electronic address ending in ".nz" gives a message a New Zealand link on its own, and sections 9, 10 and 11 apply to any message that has one. A US agency emailing a .co.nz address from a US mailbox on US infrastructure is inside the Act.
- [Cold Email Laws in Norway: Named Work Addresses Need Consent](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-norway/): October 15, 2026. Norway's Marketing Control Act bans sending marketing by email, text message, fax or automated calls to a natural person who has not agreed in advance. The Consumer Authority (Forbrukertilsynet) reads that rule to include a person's own work address, such as ola.nordmann@firma.no, even when the offer is aimed at the business and even if the address is listed as the company's contact in the Brønnøysund registers. Only addresses that do not belong to a specific person, such as post@firma.no, fall outside it. Significant or repeated breaches can bring an infringement fee. We build cold email infrastructure for B2B outreach, and this guide covers what the Norwegian rules allow and how to run a campaign that stays inside them.
- [Cold Email Laws in Pakistan: PECA's Spam Fines and Unsubscribe Rule](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-pakistan/): October 26, 2026. Pakistan has no comprehensive data protection law in force, so the rule that governs cold email is section 25 of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016 (PECA). It makes spamming an offence, including sending unsolicited information without the recipient's permission, and it requires anyone engaged in direct marketing to give recipients an option to unsubscribe. A first violation of either kind is fined up to Rs 50,000, and each later one Rs 50,000 to Rs 1,000,000. Harmful, fraudulent, misleading or illegal messages carry up to three months in prison, a fine of Rs 50,000 to Rs 5,000,000, or both. Statute text read on 26 October 2026 in the Sindh Judicial Academy's consolidated PECA (amended to 2025); bill status from the Chambers Data Protection and Privacy 2026 Pakistan chapter.
- [Cold Email Laws in the Philippines: No Spam Act, One Big Trap](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-philippines/): September 17, 2026. Outbound teams add the Philippines because it is English speaking and cheap to test, then drop it when a compliance blog says "assume GDPR, get consent." That advice is wrong twice over. The Philippines has no anti-spam statute at all, and its regulator has said in writing that cold emailing strangers is lawful. The exposure is the fields your data vendor attaches to the record, and a rule issued five months ago that reaches the companies who buy lists as well as those who scrape them. There is no Philippine CAN-SPAM, no CASL and no PECR. The Senate's subject index lists spam bills and zero Republic Acts. The two that covered email, the Spam Control Act of 2011 (SB 2900) and its 2013 refiling, proposed to control "unsolicited commercial communications sent in bulk by electronic mail," and both died in committee.
- [Cold Email Laws in Poland: Consent First, Even for B2B, or a 3% Fine](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-poland/): October 5, 2026. Cold email to Poland needs the recipient's prior consent, and since November 10, 2024 that includes a company inbox. Article 398 of the Electronic Communications Law (Prawo komunikacji elektronicznej, the Act of July 12, 2024, Journal of Laws 2024 item 1221) prohibits using telecommunications terminal equipment or automated calling systems to send commercial information, including direct marketing, to a subscriber or end user who has not agreed in advance. The President of UKE, the Office of Electronic Communications, can fine a sender that skips consent up to 3 percent of the previous calendar year's revenue or up to PLN 1,000,000, whichever is higher, under Article 446(5). The email rule it replaced, Article 10 of the 2002 Act on Providing Services by Electronic Means, protected only recipients who are natural persons; it was repealed the day the new law took effect.
- [Cold Email Laws in Portugal: Companies Opt Out, People Opt In](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-portugal/): October 15, 2026. Portugal splits its spam rule by recipient. Under article 13-A of Law 41/2004, marketing email and SMS to a private individual need that person's prior express consent, but marketing to a company is allowed until the company objects and joins a national opt-out list kept by the Directorate-General for Consumers (DGC). Senders have to check that list, which the DGC updates monthly. Breaking the rules is an administrative offence with fines of €5,000 to €5,000,000 for a company. We build cold email infrastructure, and this guide covers what the law says, where the B2B exception ends, and how to run a Portuguese campaign that stays inside it. The rules below come from the consolidated text of Law 41/2004 on the Diário da República, the DGC's list pages and the data protection authority's 2022 guideline on electronic marketing, all read 15 October 2026.
- [Cold Email Laws in Qatar: Two Regimes, Opposite Defaults](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-qatar/): September 10, 2026. Qatar is one of the few countries where the same cold email, sent to the same person, can be lawful or unlawful depending on which side of a registry line their employer sits. On the mainland, Law No. 13 of 2016 makes prior consent a precondition for any marketing email. Inside the Qatar Financial Centre, a separate rulebook lets a firm send on legitimate interests and stop only when the recipient objects. Almost no English language guide states this, and it is the first thing a sender targeting Doha needs to know. The controlling provision is Article 22 of Law No. 13 of 2016 on Protecting Personal Data Privacy, in the chapter headed Electronic Communication for the Purpose of Direct Marketing.
- [Cold Email Laws in Romania: Consent, or Fines to 2% of Turnover](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-romania/): November 2, 2026. Romania requires express prior consent for commercial email under article 12(1) of Law 506/2004, and the text makes no exception for business addresses. The exception in the text, as quoted by the EU Court of Justice in November 2025, is the existing customer rule in article 12(2). On that quotation, breaches are fined 5,000 to 100,000 lei, or up to 2% of turnover for companies above 5,000,000 lei. The regulator, ANSPDCP, announced on 6 August 2026 a 50,000 lei fine under the same article for automated sales calls made without consent. Law 506/2004 as quoted in CJEU case C-654/23 on EUR-Lex, and ANSPDCP press releases on dataprotection.ro, read on 2 November 2026.
- [Cold Email Laws Saudi Arabia: Everyone Cites the Wrong Law](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-saudi-arabia/): Cold email into Saudi Arabia is not governed mainly by the PDPL. The operative rule is the Communications, Space and Technology Commission's Regulations for Curbing SPAM Messages and Calls, and it starts from the opposite default to Europe or the United States: promotional messages are blocked for every subscriber from the outset, consent buried in a privacy policy or a service contract is expressly disregarded, and the sender carries the burden of proving consent. Short messages and calls arriving from outside the Kingdom must be service or personal only. Email is treated differently, and that difference is the whole article. Ask an AI assistant whether cold email is legal in Saudi Arabia and you will get the Personal Data Protection Law. Reasonable, and the wrong first document.
- [Cold Email Laws in Singapore: PDPA Guide (2026)](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-singapore/): Singapore is the gateway to Southeast Asia. The Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) governs all cold email. Unlike Germany's strict consent model, Singapore uses an opt-out framework, but with significant restrictions. B2B cold email is legal if you follow the rules. We're scaling into APAC markets. Singapore is first. Here's the exact legal framework and what works.
- [Cold Email Laws in South Africa: Opt-In Only, One Ask Allowed](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-south-africa/): September 5, 2026. Most guides to South African spam law still describe an opt-out regime under Section 45 of the Electronic Communications and Transactions Act: include an unsubscribe, disclose where you got the address, and you are fine. That section was repealed with effect from June 30, 2021, when the Protection of Personal Information Act took full effect and its Schedule struck Section 45 out. South Africa has been a pure opt-in jurisdiction for five years, and it is one of the few in the world where the data protection statute protects companies as well as people. The Information Regulator's first direct marketing enforcement case, against a training firm, treated a sender's habit of guessing five different email domains for one contact as evidence of unlawful collection, and said the unsubscribe link cured nothing.
- [Cold Email Laws in South Korea: Two Exceptions, and Neither Is B2B](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-south-korea/): September 22, 2026. South Korea is an opt-in market with no business-address exception. Article 50 of the Act on Promotion of Information and Communications Network Utilization and Information Protection, the Network Act, requires express prior consent before you transmit advertising information for profit through an electronic transmission medium. The statute then lists the exceptions, and there are only two. Neither of them is the one most outbound teams rely on everywhere else, which is that the address was published on the company's own website. The version read for this piece is the English translation of Act No. 20069, promulgated 23 January 2024, published by the Korea Legislation Research Institute, with the Enforcement Decree alongside it.
- [Cold Email Laws in Spain: LSSI Article 21 and the GDPR (2026)](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-spain/): Cold email to a Spanish recipient is prohibited unless you already have that recipient's prior, express permission, or you already have a contract with them and you are emailing about something similar to what they bought. There is no business-to-business carve-out. The rule sits in Article 21 of Ley 34/2002, known as the LSSI, and Spain's data protection authority, the AEPD, has held for years that this rule overrides the GDPR legal basis you would normally reach for. That last point is where almost every English-language guide gets Spain wrong. The standard advice is that business-to-business cold email is defensible across the EU under legitimate interest, GDPR Article 6.1.f, with a documented balancing test. In Spain that argument does not get you to the send button, and the AEPD said so in writing.
- [Cold Email Laws in Sweden: GDPR & Marketing Act Guide (2026)](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-sweden/): Cold Email Laws in Sweden: GDPR & Marketing Act Guide (2026) Sweden is stricter than most Nordic countries. But there's an advantage: reply rates jump to 8% when you use Swedish language and demonstrate cultural awareness. We've scaled Swedish campaigns specifically because the compliance framework is clear, and the language barrier creates less competition.
- [Cold Email Laws in Switzerland: The Penalty Is Criminal](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-switzerland/): Cold email into Switzerland is governed by the Federal Act on Unfair Competition (UCA), Article 3 paragraph 1 letter o, and not by a privacy regulator. The rule asks for three things at once: prior consent, a correct sender, and a simple free of charge way to refuse. Under Article 23 UCA a wilful breach is a criminal offence carrying a custodial sentence of up to three years or a monetary penalty, and the complaint is filed by a competitor or a customer rather than by an authority. Most teams treat Switzerland as the GDPR with a nicer flag. Switzerland is not in the EU, the GDPR is not the operative rule for your send, and the rule that is operative sits in competition law with a criminal penalty bolted to it.
- [Cold Email Laws in Thailand: PDPA Legitimate Interest, a THB 200,000 Per-Email Spam Fine and a Regulator Now Fining](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-thailand/): September 28, 2026. Thailand is one of the few markets where cold email is governed by two statutes with different logics, and a sender has to clear both. The Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562, the PDPA, became law on May 28, 2019 and came into full force on June 1, 2022 after two Royal Decree postponements; it is a GDPR-shaped privacy law with a legitimate-interest basis, an express right to object to direct marketing and administrative fines up to THB 5 million, and according to DLA Piper's country guide (updated February 14, 2026) the Personal Data Protection Committee has now imposed administrative fines in six cases, one in 2024 and five in 2025.
- [Cold Email Laws in Turkey: B2B Skips Consent, Not IYS Registration](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-turkey/): October 5, 2026. Turkey regulates commercial email under Law No. 6563 on the Regulation of Electronic Commerce, in force since May 1, 2015, and the rule splits by recipient. Article 6(1) allows commercial electronic messages only with the recipient's prior consent, given in writing or by any electronic means, while Article 6(2) lets a sender message tradesmen and merchants (esnaf and tacir) without prior consent. The B2B exemption is narrower than it looks. Under the Regulation on Commercial Communication and Commercial Electronic Messages, as amended on January 4, 2020, every sender must register with İYS, the national Message Management System, and before relying on the merchant exemption must record the merchants' addresses in İYS and check there that none has refused.
- [Cold Email Laws in the UAE: What's Legal for B2B Outreach (2026)](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-uae/): Cold Email Laws in the UAE: What's Legal for B2B Outreach (2026) We operate from Dubai. I know UAE cold email regulations from first-hand experience, and from fixing compliance mistakes across 500+ campaigns. Cold email is legal in the UAE, but the rules are different from Europe.
- [Cold Email Laws in the UK: PECR Guide (2026)](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-united-kingdom/): Cold email is legal in the UK for B2B outreach, but only under strict conditions outlined in PECR and GDPR. The key advantage is the B2B soft opt-in rule: you can send cold emails to published corporate email addresses without prior consent, as long as recipients have a clear unsubscribe option and you offer an alternative to email contact. We've identified a massive market gap in the UK, there are only 23-30 cold email agencies serving a $14 billion startup funding market. Our UK expansion has already reached 26,500+ decision-makers across 30+ countries in Europe, with UK businesses seeing 70-85% inbox placement rates. PECR is the primary UK law governing electronic marketing communications. It was enacted in 2003 to implement the EU ePrivacy Directive and remained in force after Brexit with only minor modifications.
- [Cold Email Laws in the United States: CAN-SPAM Guide (2026)](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-united-states/): Cold email is legal in the United States under the CAN-SPAM Act, which was enacted in 2003. The key difference from European regulations is that the US operates on an opt-out model rather than opt-in, meaning you can send cold emails to businesses without prior explicit consent, as long as you follow specific requirements. We've sent over 500,000+ cold emails to US targets through our platform, and strict CAN-SPAM compliance keeps our clients' servers clean and deliverability rates above 85%. The Controlling the Assault of Non-Solicited Pornography and Marketing (CAN-SPAM) Act is the US federal law governing commercial email. It applies to all commercial email, including business-to-business (B2B) outreach. Unlike GDPR or PECR, CAN-SPAM doesn't require consent before you send, it only requires that you follow specific rules once you send.
- [Cold Email Laws in Vietnam: Prior Consent, the (QC) Tag and a Three-a-Day Cap](https://imisofts.com/blog/cold-email-laws-vietnam/): September 28, 2026. Cold email to Vietnam is opt-in, and the rule is written for email specifically rather than borrowed from a privacy statute. Decree No. 91/2020/ND-CP of August 14, 2020, in force since October 1, 2020, defines an advertising email as any email introducing a product, goods or service for profit, defines a spam email as an advertising email sent without the user's prior consent, and then sets out exactly what a lawful advertising email has to look like: a tag at the start of the subject line, the advertiser's full details, an opt-out block at the end, and no more than three emails to one address in a day. There is no exception for business recipients. Two newer layers now sit on top. Since January 1, 2026 the Law on Personal Data Protection, Law No.
- [Do Cold Email Laws Apply to LinkedIn Messages? Read the Definitions](https://imisofts.com/blog/do-cold-email-laws-apply-to-linkedin-messages/): Yes, in most of the markets you sell into. Canada’s CASL, Australia’s Spam Act, the UK’s PECR and the EU’s ePrivacy Directive define the message they regulate by the account it lands in, or by whether it is stored until opened, not by whether it is email, and a LinkedIn direct message fits. In the United States, two federal courts have applied CAN-SPAM to messages inside MySpace and Facebook. I read the five texts, the CRTC’s FAQ and LinkedIn’s legal pages on 26 September 2026 because adding a LinkedIn step to a sequence built on our email infrastructure raises exactly this question. It does not move the message out of the consent rules.
- [Is AI Cold Calling Legal? Yes. Your Script Has Two Seconds.](https://imisofts.com/blog/is-ai-cold-calling-legal/): AI cold calling is legal in the United States. Almost nobody is doing it legally, and the reason has nothing to do with the AI. The plain answer: no federal rule requires you to announce that the caller is a machine. What exists instead, since February 2024, is an FCC ruling that an AI generated voice counts as an artificial voice under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act. That reclassification pulls your agent into the prerecorded message rulebook: prior express written consent before anything that sells, your registered legal business name at the top of the call, and an automated opt out within two seconds of it.
- [Is Buying B2B Email Lists Legal? Only One Country Bans the Purchase](https://imisofts.com/blog/is-buying-email-lists-legal/): September 5, 2026. Of the five jurisdictions most outbound teams sell into, exactly one makes buying an email list an offence in itself. In Australia, Section 21 of the Spam Act makes it a civil penalty contravention merely to acquire a harvested-address list or the right to use one, before a single message is sent, and Section 20 catches the vendor who supplies it. Everywhere else, liability attaches at sending: the United States asks whether the message itself broke the rules, the United Kingdom and Canada ask whether the recipient consented to hear from you specifically, and the European Union asks whether you told the person, within a month, where you got their data. The practical answer to "is buying B2B email lists legal" is therefore not yes or no.
- [Is Local Presence Dialing Legal? What Caller ID Law Requires](https://imisofts.com/blog/is-local-presence-dialing-legal/): Short answer. On our reading of federal law, yes, when the caller ID is a number your account holds, you have no intent to defraud, cause harm or wrongfully obtain anything of value, and the number shown lets anyone make a do-not-call request during regular business hours. The Truth in Caller ID rule, 47 CFR 64.1604, bans misleading or inaccurate caller ID only when it is sent "with the intent to defraud, cause harm, or wrongfully obtain anything of value", and neither it nor 64.1601 uses the words "area code" or "local presence". A second rule, 64.1601(e), binds every sales caller with no intent test: transmit caller ID, never block it, and show a number that "must permit any individual to make a do-not-call request during regular business hours".
- [Is Parallel Dialing Legal? The 15-Second and 3% Rules](https://imisofts.com/blog/is-parallel-dialing-legal/): Short answer. Neither the FCC rule nor the FTC rule we read bans parallel dialing, but FCC rules decide how you run it: 47 CFR 64.1200(a)(6) bars disconnecting an unanswered telemarketing call before 15 seconds or four rings, (a)(7) caps abandoned calls at 3% of calls answered live per campaign in each 30-day period (a call is abandoned if no live sales rep is on within two seconds of the completed greeting), and (a)(5) bars using an autodialer in a way that ties up two or more lines of one multi-line business at once. Close's Predictive Dialer abandons an answered call when no rep is free, and Apollo puts its parallel dialer's latency at about three seconds with voicemail drops on, start point not stated. The FCC asked in October 2025 whether to delete the 15-second and 3% rules; the eCFR current to 30 October 2026 still has them.
- [Is Ringless Voicemail Legal? Only With Consent. It Is a Call](https://imisofts.com/blog/is-ringless-voicemail-legal/): Ringless voicemail to a mobile number is legal only with the recipient’s consent, unless it is for an emergency. In a declaratory ruling released on 21 November 2022 (FCC 22-85), the FCC found that a message dropped straight into a mobile voicemail box is a “call” made with a prerecorded voice, so it needs prior express consent, and written consent under the FCC’s rules if it sells. On two vendors’ price lists I read on 28 October 2026, a drop costs 3.5 to 12 cents; the statute sets damages at $500 for each violation. Slybroadcast, which sells ringless voicemail, says in its FAQ that it is “less intrusive than a phone call.” In 2022 the FCC rejected a petitioner’s argument that ringless voicemail is non-invasive; as commenters and complainants explained, “consumers cannot block these messages.”
- [Is Web Scraping Legal in 2026? US, EU and UK Rules for Lead Generation](https://imisofts.com/blog/is-web-scraping-legal/): September 5, 2026. The question "is web scraping legal" has two honest answers, and lead-generation teams usually hear only the first. The first is that in the United States, scraping publicly accessible pages is very unlikely to be a federal computer crime, a position the Ninth Circuit reached in 2022 and extended to AI shopping agents in August 2026. The second is that almost every scraping company that has been sued or fined since then lost on something other than the hacking statute: breach of a site's terms, fake accounts, the copyright anti-circumvention rule, or, in Europe, the duty to tell people you hold their data. The only European enforcement case squarely about scraping LinkedIn for B2B prospecting ended not with its 240,000 euro fine but with the vendor erasing a 160-million-contact database and stopping collection entirely.
- [Telemarketing Laws by State: Calling Hours and Mini-TCPA Rules](https://imisofts.com/blog/telemarketing-laws-by-state/): October 15, 2026. Federal rules allow telemarketing calls to consumers between 8 a.m. and 9 p.m. in the called person's local time, but several states are stricter. Florida, Oklahoma and Maryland allow sales calls only from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. and cap them at three in 24 hours on the same subject. Texas starts at 9 a.m., or noon on Sunday, and requires many sellers to register and post $10,000 in security before calling or texting its residents. Virginia treats marketing texts as calls and lets each person sue for $500 to $5,000 per violation. Our TCPA-compliant AI calling service is built around these rules, and this guide sets out the hours, consent rules and penalties in each of these states, plus one calling schedule that fits all of them.

Short subject lines (3-5 words) achieve 28-35% open rates vs 18-22% for longer subject lines. Question-based CTAs ("Could we chat?") outperform hard sells ("Buy now") by 25-40% in reply rate. Send Tuesday-Thursday between 9-11am for best results. Personalization with first name increases reply rate by 12-18%, but over-personalization (excessive detail) decreases reply rate by 8-15%. Email length of 50-100 words beats both shorter and longer formats.

- [How to Scale Cold Email to 5,000 Per Day Without Burning Domains](https://imisofts.com/blog/scale-cold-email-5000-per-day/): Scaling cold email breaks agencies. Not because the strategy doesn't work, but because they scale wrong. They add more inboxes, more domains, more volume, all at once. Gmail notices, domains burn out, placement drops to 40%. Game over. Key detail: Don't add Domain 2 until Domain 1 reaches 200/day. This prevents Gmail from associating multiple cold domains to you simultaneously.

- [Maryland Telemarketing Laws: 8 to 8, 3 Calls in 24 Hours](https://imisofts.com/blog/maryland-telemarketing-laws/): Short answer. Maryland's Stop the Spam Calls Act, in force since 1 January 2024 and codified mainly at Commercial Law 14-4501 to 14-4503, requires prior express written consent before a telephone solicitation (a sales, prize, poll or sales-survey call) that uses an automated system for "the selection or dialing" of numbers or plays a recorded message. It bars solicitations between 8 p.m. and 8 a.m. in the called party's time zone and more than three to the same person in 24 hours on the same subject, "regardless of the telephone numbers used". The Act's seven exemptions, including one for business-to-business sales, sit in its consent subsection, so on our reading even an exempt caller must keep to the hours and the call cap.

- [Oklahoma Telephone Solicitation Act: 8 to 8, 3 Calls, $500](https://imisofts.com/blog/oklahoma-telephone-solicitation-act/): Short answer. Oklahoma's Telephone Solicitation Act of 2022 (15 O.S. 775C.1 to 775C.6), in force since 1 November 2022, requires prior express written consent before a sales call that uses an automated system for "the selection or dialing" of numbers or plays a recorded message. It bars solicitation calls before 8 a.m. or after 8 p.m. in the called person's time zone and more than three in 24 hours on the same subject, and a called party aggrieved by a violation can sue for actual damages or $500, whichever is greater, up to three times that if the violation was willful or knowing. Older laws add a state do not call list ($600 a year to access, per the Attorney General) and seller registration ($250 in the Attorney General's 2019 packet, plus a $10,000 bond). We earn a commission if you buy Close or Apollo through our links; Oklahoma's legislature and Attorney General pay us nothing.

- [STIR/SHAKEN Attestation: A, B, C and What Earns an A](https://imisofts.com/blog/stir-shaken-attestation/): Short answer. STIR/SHAKEN attestation is the grade the provider that signs your call gives its caller ID: A when it knows you and has verified your right to the number, B when it knows you but not the number, C when it cannot vouch for the caller. On our reading of the FCC's rules that provider sets the grade, not the business placing the call, and none of the Close, Apollo or HighLevel help pages we read names a grade. On Twilio's rules (Twilio is Apollo's telephony provider and, on our reading, Close's), an A needs an approved Business Profile and SHAKEN/STIR Trust Product with the number assigned to both, and a non-Twilio number tops out at B; neither Close nor Apollo says how its own registration or business profile maps to those steps. The FCC proposed on 20 May 2026 (FCC 26-32) to codify the grades; we found no final order as of 6 November 2026.
- [TCPA Autodialer Definition: Is a Power Dialer an ATDS?](https://imisofts.com/blog/tcpa-autodialer-definition/): Short answer. Under federal law, an autodialer (an "automatic telephone dialing system", or ATDS) is equipment with the capacity to store or produce telephone numbers "using a random or sequential number generator" and to dial them. The Supreme Court settled that reading in Facebook v. Duguid on 1 April 2021, and in 2022 the Ninth Circuit held that an autodialer "must generate and dial random or sequential telephone numbers", finding no autodialer where a sequential number generator was alleged only to pick the order in which to text customers who had given their numbers. On that one court's test, a dialer that only calls a saved list does not meet the definition, on our reading, though the test turns on what the system can do.

Thinkific's cheapest plan on its public pricing page is now Start at $109 a month, or $978 a year on yearly billing (shown as $82 a month). The Basic plan, listed at $54 a month ($40 a month billed yearly) in a 5 October 2026 capture of the page, was gone by a 22 October capture, and a $499 Expand plan now sits between Grow and the sales-led Plus tier. For a new customer that roughly doubles the entry price: +$55 a month, or +$503 a year. - [Speed to Lead: What the Research Says About the First Hour](https://imisofts.com/blog/speed-to-lead/): Short answer. Speed to lead is the time between a person raising a hand, by filling in a form, calling or starting a chat, and your first real attempt to talk to them. The strongest published evidence we could check says the chance of qualifying a lead drops sharply after the first hour. In research published in Harvard Business Review, firms that tried to contact a lead within an hour were nearly 7 times as likely to qualify it as firms that waited even one more hour, and more than 60 times as likely as firms that waited a day or longer. Most teams are still slow: in a test RevenueHero published in March 2024, only 365 of 1,000 B2B websites replied to a demo request at all, and the average reply took 1 day, 5 hours and 17 minutes. Set a target in minutes, measure it from your CRM's timestamps, and make sure any automated or AI call you use to get there has the consent the law requires.
- [SaaS Lead Generation: Channels, Costs and the AI Shortlist](https://imisofts.com/blog/saas-lead-generation/): Short answer. SaaS lead generation now starts before a buyer reaches your website. In G2's March 2026 survey of 1,076 software buyers, 51% said they start research in an AI chatbot more often than in Google, against 29% in G2's 2025 Buyer Behavior Report, and G2's 2026 Buyer Behavior Report found that review sites (38%) and AI chatbots (37%) are the two biggest influences on a shortlist. A plan that works has three layers: be the answer where buyers research, capture the people who raise a hand and reply within minutes, and run outbound to the accounts that fit but have not raised a hand yet. Paid search fills the gaps at a price: LocaliQ's 2026 benchmarks put the average search ad lead at $66.69 across industries and $93.69 for business services.
- [Real Estate Lead Generation Cost: Zillow vs Ads vs Referrals](https://imisofts.com/blog/real-estate-lead-generation-cost/): Short answer. Real estate leads are priced in two ways: per lead, or as a share of your commission when a deal closes. Per lead, LocaliQ's 2026 benchmarks put a Facebook lead for real estate at $13.74 and a search ad lead for a residential agent at $157.59. Per closing, Zillow Preferred takes a success fee of 15% to 40% of your side's commission on buyer connections in the markets we checked, and 40% on any home of $400,000 or more; Zillow's old Premier Agent Flex pricing page now redirects to it. On NAR's September 2026 median price of $417,500 and Redfin's 2.52% average buyer's agent commission for homes under $500,000, that fee is about $4,208 per closing. Your own past clients cost no media spend at all, and 91% of buyers told NAR they would use their agent again or recommend them.
- [Demand Generation vs Lead Generation: Which to Fund First](https://imisofts.com/blog/demand-generation-vs-lead-generation/): Short answer. Demand generation makes the right buyers know and prefer you before they need you; lead generation collects the details of people who are ready to talk now. You need both, and two numbers explain why. Research by John Dawes of the Ehrenberg-Bass Institute, published by LinkedIn's B2B Institute, estimates that only about 5% of B2B buyers are in the market at any one time. And in 6sense's 2025 survey of more than 4,000 buyers, 94% of buying groups had ranked their preferred vendors before first contact and then bought from that favorite 77% of the time. Lead generation harvests the 5% who are buying now; demand generation decides whether you are on the list when the other 95% start.
- [Business Process Automation: Where to Start and What It Costs](https://imisofts.com/blog/business-process-automation/): Short answer. Business process automation (BPA) means running a repeatable, rule-based process, such as routing a new lead, sending an invoice or onboarding a client, through software instead of by hand, with people stepping in only for exceptions and judgment calls. The paid plans are inexpensive: Zapier's Professional plan starts at $19.99 a month on annual billing, n8n's hosted Starter plan is $20 a month with 2,500 workflow executions, and Microsoft Power Automate Premium is $15 per user a month, paid yearly. The work they replace is not: the median bookkeeping, accounting and auditing clerk earned $24.36 an hour in 2025, according to the US Bureau of Labor Statistics. Start with the process that is high in volume, low in judgment and costly when it goes wrong, and measure the hours it takes before you build anything.

Existing customers move to them at their first renewal on or after 1 November 2026, and annual customers keep their current price until their term renews. On yearly billing the rise is 13.1% to 37.6% for Lite, and Pro runs from 1.5% cheaper to 48.3% dearer. We earn a commission if you buy Kit through our links; beehiiv pays us nothing.
- [10DLC Registration Cost: $19.50 to $61, Then $1.50 to $10 a Month](https://imisofts.com/blog/10dlc-registration-cost/): Short answer. Each campaign then costs $1.50 to $10 a month, so a low-volume brand with one $10 campaign pays $139.50 in its first year before it sends a text. - [Lifetime Deal vs Subscription: The Break-Even Math for 2026](https://imisofts.com/blog/lifetime-deal-vs-subscription/): Buy the lifetime deal when the payback period is short and the job the tool does is boring. Keep the subscription when the tool has to keep moving. That much every guide agrees on. What almost none of them tell you is that the standard break-even formula is missing a term, and the missing term is the only one that can cost you the whole purchase price. The formula everyone publishes is deal price divided by monthly price equals months to break even. It is arithmetically correct and it is incomplete, because it silently assumes your downside is zero. It is not zero. On AppSumo, the largest lifetime deal marketplace, exactly how much you get back when a tool shuts down is published, it varies from 100 percent to nothing, and it depends on three things most buyers never check before they click.

- [Lifetime Deals for Agencies 2026: The License Tier Trap](https://imisofts.com/blog/lifetime-deals-for-agencies-2026/): Short version: lifetime deals are a legitimate way for an agency to cut software costs, but the number that decides whether a deal is a good buy is not the price. That is not a hidden fee and it is not a scandal: almost all of it is resellable. It is only a cost if you forgot to price it into the retainer. - [Shopify App Development Cost in 2026: The Four Fees No Quote Includes](https://imisofts.com/blog/shopify-app-development-cost-2026/): No blog post can quote you a Shopify app build price, and every guide that tries is quoting its own rate card. What can be pinned down is the part Shopify itself publishes, and that is exactly the part most budgets get wrong. The build fee is a one-time number you negotiate. Shopify's fees are a permanent number you inherit. Verified on Shopify's own developer documentation on August 6, 2026: registering to sell on the Shopify App Store costs a one-time $19 per Partner account. Revenue share is 0% on your first $1,000,000 of gross app revenue earned since January 1, 2025, then 15% above that. Separately, all billing carries a 2.9% processing fee, plus applicable sales tax.
- [Is Apollo.io Worth It in 2026? An Honest Cost and ROI Breakdown](https://imisofts.com/blog/is-apollo-worth-it-2026/): Short answer: yes, Apollo.io is still worth it in 2026 for most teams that actually do outbound, and it is still one of the best value buys in its category. Two caveats have grown teeth since we first published this guide: Apollo's credit is now the meter for almost everything the platform does, not just for revealing a contact, and its self-serve plans are licensed for internal use only, which matters if you are an agency handing lead lists to clients. It stays a clear yes if your ideal customers are mostly in the US and you verify your lists before you send. Apollo says over 600,000 companies use it, and its pricing page shows 4.7 out of 5 from 9,690 reviews, so this is not a bet on an unknown tool. The question is whether it is worth the money for your situation.
- [Is GoHighLevel Worth It in 2026? The Honest Break-Even Math](https://imisofts.com/blog/is-gohighlevel-worth-it-2026/): Short answer: GoHighLevel is worth it if you bill clients or run several businesses at once, because the break-even is low and rebilling plus tool-consolidation savings turn the subscription into profit fast. It is usually not worth it if you run one simple business and just want a single polished tool, because you will pay for an agency platform you will not fully use. The real question is not "is it good," it is "does the math work for your situation." This guide does that math with current 2026 numbers. For the full feature breakdown see our GoHighLevel review for 2026, and for the line-by-line price list see the GoHighLevel pricing guide. Here we focus only on whether it pays for itself.
